# Rustify — Architectural Migration & Memory-Safe Interop Discipline

Translating source files line-by-line from C, C++, Go, or Python into Rust produces "C/Go in Rust syntax": ubiquitous `Arc<Mutex<T>>` wrappers, raw `*mut T` pointer arithmetic, `.unwrap()` panic landmines, silent `as` integer truncations, and broken Application Binary Interface (`ABI`) layouts. `rustify` governs cross-language transformation so ownership, lifetimes, binary layout invariants, and zero-panic guarantees are locked in incrementally with compiler and runtime proof.

---

## 1. Adjacent-Skill Boundaries & Co-Loading Map

* **vs. `skills/refactoring/SKILL.md` & `skills/sweetspot/SKILL.md`:** Use `refactoring` when restructuring code that is *already* in Rust with zero contract shift, and use `sweetspot` when profiling/optimizing an already-working Rust crate (`--time`, `--memory`, `--disk`, `--net`). Never mix premature Single Instruction, Multiple Data (`SIMD`) or custom-allocator micro-tuning into the initial cross-language migration pass.
* **vs. `skills/dependency-upgrade/SKILL.md`:** Use `dependency-upgrade` when bumping crate versions in `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` or upgrading the Rust toolchain edition (`2021` -> `2024`) within an existing Rust project.
* **vs. `skills/renew/SKILL.md` (Handoff vs. Co-Load):**
  * *Active/buildable C, C++, Go, or Python module -> Rust:* Use `rustify` directly.
  * *Obsolete/unbuildable 15+ year legacy software or classic game revived into a Rust target stack:* **Co-load** `skills/renew/SKILL.md` with `rustify`: combine both Stage 1 autopsies and a single merged Stage 2 contract gate (`<= 4` questions), pin once in Stage 3, apply `renew` Stage 4.2 legacy vulnerability sanitization (plus `renew` Section 6 for classic games) alongside `rustify` Stage 4, and pass both Stage 5 gates.
* **On-Demand Reference Modules (Load Only What Matches the Source Language):**
  * *C, C++, `#![no_std]` firmware, hardware registers, or Foreign Function Interface (`FFI`) bridges:* Read [references/c-cpp-abi-and-embedded.md](./references/c-cpp-abi-and-embedded.md).
  * *Go services/concurrency or Python `PyO3` / `maturin` extensions:* Read [references/managed-go-python.md](./references/managed-go-python.md).
* **Co-Loaded Capabilities When Applicable:**
  * *Compiled-only `.so` / `.dll` / `.a` / firmware binaries lacking source:* Co-load `reverse-engineer-anything` (`rea_rea` Model Context Protocol (`MCP`) server when available) to extract symbol graphs and calling conventions first.
  * *Domain type & typestate design:* Apply `skills/mistake-proofing/SKILL.md` and `skills/mistake-proofing/languages.md` (`Rust` section: `Prevented` vs. `Announced`).
  * *Multi-window (`>8` files) migrations:* Partition via `skills/marathon/SKILL.md` (`W1: Characterization & Leaf Types`, `W2: Interop Seam & Intermediate Logic`, `W3: Unsafe Purification & Audit`). Record target profile and binary layout decisions via `skills/architecture-decision-records/SKILL.md`.

---

## 2. Stage 1 — Silent Build, Layout & Dependency Autopsy (Before Asking Questions)

Never ask the user technical facts already visible in the repository (`GEMINI.md` Rule 11). First audit `Makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `meson.build`, `compile_commands.json`, `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, and any `build.rs` via `read_file` before executing `make`, `cmake`, `pytest`, `maturin`, or `cargo check` (because `cargo check` compiles and runs `build.rs` and procedural macros with full user privileges; `GEMINI.md` Rule 12). Map symbol dependencies via `python3 scripts/code_map.py profile <symbol>` / `blast-radius <symbol>` to establish:

1. **Source Language Dialect & Build Seam:** Compiler flags (`-fno-strict-aliasing`, `-fwrapv`, `-ffast-math` / `-ffp-contract`, C/C++ standard, target triple/endianness), `setjmp`/`longjmp` or C++ exception paths, static vs. shared linkage, and existing test runners (`ctest`, `gtest`, `pytest`, `go test`).
2. **Binary & Hardware Coupling:** Structs crossing wire, file, shared-memory, or Memory-Mapped Input/Output (`MMIO`) boundaries; interrupt service routines; thread/lock topology; and global mutable state.
3. **Dependency Graph (`Leaf -> Intermediate -> Root`):**
   * *Leaf Nodes:* Constants, binary/math kernels, checksums, and stateless data types with zero external calls.
   * *Intermediate Nodes:* Parsers, state machines, codecs, and domain validators.
   * *Root Nodes:* Input/Output (`I/O`) loops, thread/async orchestrators, and hardware interrupt handlers. External `FFI` entry points also sit at the root boundary.

---

## 3. Stage 2 — The Migration Contract Gate (`ask_question`, Max 3 Decisions)

Unless the user's prompt already specifies every axis below, ask **at most 3 pointed questions** via `ask_question` (with `(Recommended)` defaults grounded in Stage 1; in exported runtimes lacking `ask_question`, emit at most `3` numbered plain-text questions with `2–3` options and `1` `(Recommended)` default per question, then stop for user input):

1. **Target Profile:**
   * *`standard-service`:* Full `std`, structured errors (`thiserror` at library seams, `anyhow` at application roots), and bounded concurrency (`tokio` / `rayon` where needed).
   * *`embedded-no-std`:* `#![no_std]` (decoupled as `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]` on pure domain crates for host testing, with `alloc` only if authorized), deterministic fixed-capacity buffers (`heapless`), `embedded-hal` traits, and `critical-section` interrupt synchronization.
   * *`safety-critical` (automotive ISO 26262 / avionics DO-178C / MISRA-aligned):* Strict `#![no_std]`, zero dynamic heap allocation after initialization, **Zero-Panic Guarantee** on production targets (no `.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, `panic!()`, `todo!()`, or unchecked `slice[i]`), and bounded formal proof harnesses.
2. **Cutover & Interop Strategy:**
   * *`idiomatic-rewrite`:* Replace the target module or binary end-to-end in pure safe Rust while preserving external command-line, wire, or file contracts.
   * *`incremental-ffi` (Strangler Bridge):* Keep the host application running and replace one module at a time behind a verified `ABI` seam. Use `bindgen` + `cbindgen` for C headers, `cxx` for C++ classes/templates, `PyO3` + `maturin` for Python, or a C static/shared seam for Go `cgo`.
3. **Legacy Defect, Overflow & Float Policy:** Confirm whether silent source-language quirks (C unsigned wraparound, sentinel error codes, loose input acceptance, or fused floating-point contraction drift vs. `0` Units in the Last Place (`ULP`) with `-ffp-contract=off`) must be preserved bit-for-bit or tightened into explicit `Authorized Sanitization Transitions`.

Pin every added Cargo crate (`=x.y.z` + `Cargo.lock`, `--locked`) or external build dependency to an exact version or 40-character commit hash (`GEMINI.md` Rule 12), and lock confirmed choices into `AC-1..N` acceptance criteria (`skills/harness/SKILL.md` §4.E) before writing production code.

---

## 4. Stage 3 — Differential Pinning & Leaf-to-Root Redesign

1. **Pin Source Oracle First (`skills/refactoring/SKILL.md` §3 & `skills/test-design/SKILL.md`):**
   * Capture golden edge-case vectors from the untouched source implementation (empty/zero-length buffers, boundary integers `0`, `INT_MIN`, `INT_MAX`, `UINT_MAX`, malformed frames, non-UTF-8 byte sequences) or record a `file:line` **Equivalence Ledger** in `scratch/equivalence_ledger.md` when the source target cannot execute locally.
   * **Immutable Cross-Language Test Discipline (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9):** Never delete, comment out, or weaken existing C, C++, Go, or Python test suites to pass a gate. Keep superseded legacy test files on disk and running across `incremental-ffi` seams until replacement Rust public-seam and differential tests are green, the user authorizes `## Authorized Test Modifications` in `tasks.md` (`[Legacy Test Transition Request]`), and the human operator seals a fresh `agy-guard test-boundary snapshot`.
2. **Redesign Data Models Before Function Bodies (`skills/mistake-proofing/languages.md`):**
   * Replace nullable pointers and magic sentinels (`NULL`, `-1`, `nil`, `None`) with `Option<T>` (`Option<&T>` / `Option<&mut T>` / `NonNull<T>` inside low-level wrappers).
   * Replace `errno`, out-parameters, and unchecked exceptions with `#[must_use]` `Result<T, DomainError>` enums, using `Vec::try_reserve_exact` plus explicit byte-cap bounds on untrusted wire lengths so corrupt lengths return `Err(...)` instead of aborting on allocation failure.
   * Replace invalid flag combinations and deep Object-Oriented Programming (`OOP`) inheritance hierarchies with closed algebraic `enum` variants, flat structs, composition, and focused traits (`Prevented` at compile time).
3. **Execute Strictly Leaf-to-Root in Narrow Vertical Slices:** Port and verify leaf types and pure kernels first (`<= 3` tightly coupled files, such as header/implementation/bridge, per planned forward migration slice — an explicit `GEMINI.md` Rule 13 forward-slice carve-out, while unverified bug-fix retry loops after a failing gate remain strictly capped at `GEMINI.md` Rule 13's `max(1 file, ~10%)`). Next port intermediate state machines and parsers, and wire root `I/O` loops or external `FFI` glue last so ownership and lifetime shapes stabilize from the inside out.

---

## 5. Stage 4 — Two-Stage `unsafe` Purification & Six Red Lines

When porting pointer-heavy C/C++ or hardware code, never combine behavioral translation and `unsafe` refactoring in one unverified leap:

1. **Stage A (Behavioral Parity Seam):** Establish a compiling, test-pinned slice behind a narrow private `unsafe` boundary and prove parity against Stage 3 golden vectors.
2. **Stage B (Safe Purification):** Systematically shrink and eliminate `unsafe` blocks by replacing raw pointer + length pairs (`const T* ptr, size_t len`) with borrowed slices (`&[T]`, `&mut [T]`), iterators, checked slice splits (`split_at_mut`), or arena indices (`Vec<Node>` + typed index newtypes instead of cyclic/intrusive pointer graphs).
3. **Mandatory Invariant Documentation:** Every remaining unavoidable `unsafe` block (foreign call, `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` register access, or zero-copy layout cast not covered by `bytemuck`/`zerocopy`) must sit inside a minimal private safe wrapper. Each `unsafe` block and `unsafe impl` must carry an explicit `// SAFETY:` comment stating the exact preconditions verified at the boundary.

### Six Strictly Prohibited Anti-Patterns (Red Lines)
1. **The `Arc<Mutex<T>>` / `Rc<RefCell<T>>` Reflex:** Never wrap every ported struct in shared interior mutability to silence the borrow checker. Assign a single owner, pass `&T` / `&mut T` down the call tree, or transfer ownership over bounded channels.
2. **Hidden Panics as Error Handling:** Never translate C error codes, Go `err != nil`, or Python exceptions into `.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, or unchecked `buf[idx]`. Use `.get(idx).ok_or(...)?` and explicit error variants.
3. **Silent Narrowing `as` Casts & Blind Overflow Rules:** Never narrow integers with `val as u16`; use `u16::try_from(val)?`. Distinguish intentional C `unsigned` modular arithmetic (`wrapping_add`, `Wrapping<u32>`) from bug-prone arithmetic (`checked_add`, `saturating_sub`)—blindly converting intentional checksum/crypto wraparound to `checked_add` breaks parity.
4. **Unannotated Cross-Boundary Struct Layouts:** Never pass a default `repr(Rust)` struct across `FFI`, shared memory, or binary wire/register maps because `rustc` reorders fields freely. Enforce explicit `#[repr(C)]` or `#[repr(transparent)]` plus compile-time size/offset assertions (see [references/c-cpp-abi-and-embedded.md](./references/c-cpp-abi-and-embedded.md)).
5. **Bidirectional Unwinding Across Foreign Boundaries:** Panicking from Rust across `extern "C"`—or letting C `longjmp` or uncaught C++ exceptions jump across Rust frames holding `Drop` destructors—triggers immediate Undefined Behavior (`UB`). Guard `std` Rust exports with `std::panic::catch_unwind` (`#![no_std]` exports enforce `panic = "abort"` plus static panic-freedom lints, while `PyO3` extension wheels keep `panic = "unwind"`), and trap C `setjmp`/`longjmp` or C++ `try-catch` strictly inside thin C/C++ shims before returning error codes to Rust.
6. **Premature Lifetime Proliferation & Blind UTF-8 Assumptions:** Prefer owned fields in domain structs and borrowed slices (`&[u8]`, `&str`) in parameters unless measured zero-copy parsing requires `'a`; never call `.to_str()?` on raw C `CStr` / OS path bytes unless strict UTF-8 validity is part of the proven contract.

---

## 6. Stage 5 — Three-Tier Verification Ladder & Independent Auditor Gate

Treat deterministic Rust and native toolchains as mandatory co-verifiers (routing `>500`-line or twice-failing borrow-checker/trait traces to the `build-error-resolver` subagent per `skills/harness/SKILL.md` §3.B):

### Tier V1 — Mandatory Universal Compiler, Lint & Differential Parity Gate
Run on every slice and before delivery (for `#![no_std]` hardware crates, scope `--target <embedded-triple>` to `--lib --bins` and run unit tests on the `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]` domain crate with `--target <host-triple>`):
```bash
cargo check --all-targets
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks
cargo test
```
* Under `safety-critical` profiles, enforce panic/truncation bans on **production targets** (`cargo clippy --lib --bins -- -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic -D clippy::indexing_slicing -D clippy::ptr_as_ptr -D clippy::cast_possible_truncation`) so `assert!` / `assert_eq!` macros inside `#[test]` targets remain valid.
* Execute all Stage 3 golden-vector and cross-language differential parity suites within the agreed integer/float tolerance to `100%` pass.

### Tier V2 — Mandatory Memory & Boundary Sanitizer Gate (Whenever `unsafe` or Foreign Interop Exists)
* **Pure-Rust `unsafe` blocks:** Run `cargo +nightly miri test` to catch aliasing (`Stacked` / `Tree Borrows`), uninitialized memory reads, alignment violations, and out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic.
* **Mixed C/C++ <-> Rust binaries:** Because `miri` cannot execute external C/C++ functions, compile and run the linked integration test binary with `AddressSanitizer` and `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer` enabled on the C/C++ toolchain alongside `>= 1,000` `proptest` cases or `>= 10,000` `cargo fuzz` runs (`>= 30 s`) over boundary inputs.

### Tier V3 — Safety-Critical Bounded Formal Verification Gate (`cargo kani`)
* For `safety-critical` and `embedded-no-std` kernels/wrappers, check `command -v cargo-kani`: when installed, author `#[kani::proof]` harnesses proving panic-freedom, bounds safety, and invariant preservation across bounded symbolic inputs (`cargo kani`).
* **Fail-Closed Verification Gap Rule (`GEMINI.md` Rule 8):** When `miri` or sanitizers on newly introduced `unsafe` / interop seams—or `cargo-kani` under a `safety-critical` profile—cannot execute on the host, declare the exact unrun sensor and seam in the `Verification Gap Declaration` and halt delivery in `BLOCKED` status pending user review (never claim formal proof from `cargo test` alone; avoid fragile `Prusti` gates unless already pinned by the repository).

### Pre-Delivery Auditor Dispatch & Delivery Block
Before declaring completion on `FFI`, `unsafe`, public binary or programming interface changes, `safety-critical` profiles, or `>8`-file migrations (`GEMINI.md` §3 Critical Exceptions), dispatch the read-only `security-boundary-verifier`, `silent-failure-hunter`, `contract-change-auditor`, and `test-adequacy-auditor` subagents (plus `consistency-auditor` and `specification-gap-auditor` on `safety-critical` specifications). In the `GEMINI.md` Rule 5/8 Delivery Block, report: the active Target Profile & Interop Strategy, differential parity test counts, remaining `unsafe` block count with `file:line` `// SAFETY:` coordinates, executed verification tiers (`V1` / `V2` / `V3`), and any host-unavailable formal or hardware checks.

# C, C++, Application Binary Interface & Embedded Rust Migration Reference

On-demand companion to `skills/rustify/SKILL.md` for C, C++, `#![no_std]` firmware, hardware drivers, Application Binary Interface (`ABI`) contracts, and mixed-binary Foreign Function Interface (`FFI`) migrations.

---

## 1. C and C++ -> Idiomatic Rust Architectural Matrix

| C / C++ Pattern | Idiomatic Rust Replacement | Soundness & Architectural Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `const T*` / `T*` (non-null single item) | `&T` / `&mut T` | Enforces shared read-only or exclusive mutable aliasing at compile time. |
| `T*` (nullable pointer) | `Option<&T>`, `Option<&mut T>`, or `Option<NonNull<T>>` | Niche optimization gives `Option<&T>` and `Option<fn(...)>` the exact pointer size of C `T*` with zero null-dereference hazard. |
| `const T* buf, size_t len` | `&[T]` (or `&mut [T]` for mutable buffers) | Fat slice bundles base pointer and element count; construct at `FFI` entry only after verifying non-null, alignment, initialized elements, and `len * size_of::<T>() <= isize::MAX` (`std::slice::from_raw_parts` preconditions). |
| `char*` (`NUL`-terminated string) | `&CStr` / `CString` -> `&[u8]` (or `&str` only if UTF-8 is guaranteed) | C strings have no UTF-8 invariant; calling `.to_str()?` blindly rejects valid binary/Latin-1 C inputs. Parse bytes via `CStr::to_bytes()` first. |
| `malloc` / `free` / `std::unique_ptr<T>` | Stack `T` or `Box<T>` (`Drop`) | Deterministic Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (`RAII`). Never call `Box::from_raw`, `CString::from_raw`, `Vec::from_raw_parts`, or cross-module `libc::free` on a foreign heap pointer—allocator mismatch triggers immediate Undefined Behavior (`UB`), so wrap the foreign module's own destructor function inside a custom `Drop` newtype instead. |
| `std::shared_ptr<T>` | Single owner + `&T` borrows, or `Arc<T>` across threads | Refactor ownership hierarchy first; reach for `Arc<T>` only for genuine concurrent shared lifetime. |
| `void* user_data` callback context | Generic `<F: FnMut(...)>` or `Box<Box<dyn Trait>>` thin pointer | Passing `Box<dyn Trait>` directly as `*mut c_void` corrupts pointers because `dyn Trait` is a 2-word fat pointer! Double-box (`Box::into_raw(Box::new(boxed_trait))`) or monomorphize a generic trampoline `extern "C" fn<T>`. |
| Intrusive / cyclic doubly linked lists | `Vec<Node>` + typed index handle (`SlotKey` / `usize`) | Eliminates self-referential lifetimes and dangling node pointers while improving cache locality. |
| C `goto cleanup;` / C++ `try-catch` | `Result<T, E>`, `?`, and scoped `Drop` guards (`scopeguard` if needed) | Makes every cleanup path deterministic without forgotten label jumps or unwinding across C frames. |
| `#define` constants, bitmasks & function macros | Typed `const`, `bitflags`-style newtypes, and `#[inline]` generics | Type-checked at compile time without double-evaluation macro bugs. |

### Foreign Handle Thread-Safety Classification (`Send` / `Sync`)
Raw pointers (`*const T`, `*mut T`, `NonNull<T>`) are `!Send` and `!Sync` in Rust for a reason. Never slap `unsafe impl Send` or `unsafe impl Sync` onto a foreign handle wrapper merely to appease `tokio::spawn` or `PyO3`:
1. **Thread-Affine Foreign Handle (`!Send + !Sync`):** Default when C state uses thread-local storage, single-threaded contexts, or undocumented locking; retain `PhantomData<*const ()>` (`#[pyclass(unsendable)]` in `PyO3`).
2. **Externally Synchronized / Movable Handle (`unsafe impl Send`, `!Sync`):** Permitted only when upstream C documentation guarantees the handle may transfer across OS threads so long as access is exclusive (`&mut self` or wrapped in a `Mutex`).
3. **Concurrently Thread-Safe Handle (`unsafe impl Send + unsafe impl Sync`):** Permitted only when upstream C documentation guarantees internal atomic/mutex synchronization across concurrent callers; cite the exact C contract inside each `// SAFETY:` block.

---

## 2. Binary Layout, Alignment, Bitfields & Integer Semantics

1. **Struct Layout & Padding (`#[repr(C)]`):**
   * Rust's default `repr(Rust)` has unspecified field order and padding. Any struct crossing `FFI`, `mmap`, network headers, or binary file records **must** declare `#[repr(C)]` (or `#[repr(transparent)]` for single-field newtypes), including Direct Memory Access (`DMA`) descriptors.
   * Add compile-time layout assertions (`const _: () = assert!(core::mem::size_of::<Frame>() == 16);` and `core::mem::offset_of!`) matching C `sizeof` / `offsetof`.
   * **Packed Struct Hazard (`#[repr(C, packed)]`):** Never take a reference (`&packed.field`) to an unaligned field inside a `packed` struct—creating an unaligned `&T` is immediate `UB` even without dereferencing it! Copy scalar fields out by value (`let v = packed.field;`) or use `core::ptr::addr_of!(packed.field).read_unaligned()`.
   * **C Bitfields & Foreign `enum` Discriminants:** Rust has no C-compatible bitfield syntax because C bitfield bit-ordering and container straddling are compiler/target ABI-specific; model bitfields as explicit fixed-width integers (`u8` / `u16` / `u32` or audited `bitflags` wrappers) with shift/mask accessors verified by cross-language `sizeof` and bit-pattern differential tests. Never accept a bare `#[repr(C)] enum` directly as an `extern "C"` input parameter from untrusted C callers: C `enum` width varies under `-fshort-enums` and passing an out-of-range integer bit pattern into a Rust `enum` causes instant `UB`—accept the raw fixed-width integer (`c_int` / `u32`) or a `#[repr(transparent)]` integer newtype and convert via `TryFrom`.
   * **Zero-Copy Byte Casting:** Prefer `zerocopy` or `bytemuck` (`Pod`, `Zeroable`, `FromBytes`) over raw `transmute` / `*const Header` casts so padding-byte and invalid-bit-pattern `UB` are rejected at compile time.
2. **C Integer Promotion & Signed vs. Unsigned Overflow:**
   * In C, `uint8_t` and `uint16_t` promote implicitly to signed `int` before arithmetic (`(uint16_t)a * (uint16_t)b` can trigger signed 32-bit overflow `UB` in C!). Make intermediate widths explicit in Rust (`u32::from(a) * u32::from(b)`).
   * C `unsigned` overflow is defined modulo $2^N$ (`a.wrapping_add(b)`), whereas C `signed` overflow is `UB`. Audit hashes, ring-buffer indices, timers, and Cyclic Redundancy Checks (`CRC`) carefully: use `wrapping_*` where modular wraparound is the algorithm, `checked_*` where overflow indicates corrupt input, and `saturating_*` for clamped control loops.

---

## 3. Interop Toolchain Selection (`bindgen` / `cbindgen` vs. `cxx`)

Choose the interop layer from the actual `ABI` boundary discovered in Stage 1:

* **Pure C Boundary (`.h` headers, C hosts, dynamic plugins, or Real-Time Operating System (`RTOS`) kernels):**
  * *Calling C from Rust:* Generate raw bindings in a dedicated `*-sys` module/crate via `bindgen` (allowlisting specific functions/types), capture OS thread-local error state (`std::io::Error::last_os_error()` for `errno` / Windows `GetLastError`) immediately on the calling thread before any allocation, `Drop`, or `.await`, and expose **only** a safe Rust wrapper seam above `*-sys`. If the C library uses `setjmp`/`longjmp`, trap `setjmp` inside a thin C wrapper function before returning an error code to Rust—never allow `longjmp` to jump across Rust stack frames.
  * *Calling Rust from C:* Expose `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C" fn ...` taking opaque handle pointers or `#[repr(C)]` structs, guard unwinding (`std::panic::catch_unwind` on `std` or `panic = "abort"` on `#![no_std]`), preserve expected `errno` contracts when shimming legacy C functions, pair every `*_new` allocator export with a matching Rust `*_free` export, and generate the C header deterministically via `cbindgen`.
* **Modern C++ Boundary (classes, namespaces, `std::unique_ptr`, `std::vector`, `std::string`, `rust::Slice`):**
  * Prefer **`cxx`** (`#[cxx::bridge]`) over raw `extern "C"` glue: `cxx` statically verifies both the Rust and C++ signatures at build time, catches C++ exceptions into `Result<T, cxx::Exception>` without unwinding across Rust `Drop` frames, and prevents mismatched struct layouts without manual `*mut c_void` casts. Evaluate `autocxx` only when ingesting large existing C++ header surfaces that cannot be wrapped behind a narrow `#[cxx::bridge]` facade.
* **Mixed Build & Sanitizer Wiring (`CMake` / `Meson` / `Cargo`):**
  * Integrate Cargo crates into CMake builds via `Corrosion` pinned to an exact release tag + 40-character Git commit hash (`GEMINI.md` Rule 12), or compile C/C++ shims via the pinned `cc` crate inside `build.rs`.
  * In `incremental-ffi` projects, run the combined C/C++ + Rust test binary with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` (matching compiler sanitizer runtimes when testing cross-language memory ownership).

---

## 4. `#![no_std]`, Embedded Hardware & Safety-Critical Rules

When `target_profile` is `embedded-no-std` or `safety-critical`:

1. **Host-Testable Crate Split & Deterministic Allocation:** Structure pure protocol/math/state-machine logic in a `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]` core crate so `cargo test`, `miri`, and `cargo kani` execute cleanly on the host, keeping board/register glue in a thin `#![no_std]` hardware crate (`cargo check --lib --bins --target <triple>`). Forbid unbounded recursion and dynamic `alloc` after boot unless authorized in Stage 2; use `heapless::Vec<T, N>` / `heapless::Deque<T, N>` or caller-supplied `&mut [u8]` arenas returning `Error::CapacityExceeded`.
2. **Hardware Register & `volatile` Semantics:** Never model Memory-Mapped Input/Output (`MMIO`) registers as `&mut RegBlock` references—the Rust compiler may insert spurious reads or elide repeated writes on `&mut T`! Access hardware registers exclusively via `svd2rust` / `ral` Peripheral Access Crates (`PAC`), `volatile-register`, or raw pointer `core::ptr::read_volatile` / `core::ptr::write_volatile` (`addr_of_mut!`).
3. **Interrupt & Concurrency Soundness:** Never use raw `static mut` (instant aliasing hazard on re-entrant interrupts). Share state between Interrupt Service Routines (`ISR`) and main loops via `core::sync::atomic::Atomic*` (with explicit `Ordering` rationale) or `critical_section::Mutex<RefCell<Option<T>>>`.
4. **Panic Handler & Binary Footprint:** Configure an explicit deterministic `#[panic_handler]` in the binary/hardware crate (safe hardware fault state + halt/reset, avoiding multi-kilobyte `core::fmt` formatting on constrained microcontrollers; `defmt` when telemetry is used) and verify zero `core::panicking` symbols remain on hot safety-critical paths when required (`cargo bloat` / `llvm-objdump` or `cargo kani` bounded proofs).

# Go & Python -> Rust Migration and Interop Reference

On-demand companion to `skills/rustify/SKILL.md` for migrating or bridging garbage-collected Go services and dynamic Python modules (`PyO3` + `maturin`) into idiomatic Rust.

---

## 1. Go -> Idiomatic Rust Architectural Matrix

| Go Pattern | Idiomatic Rust Replacement | Soundness & Architectural Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Returning heap pointers (`return &Config{...}`) | Return owned value (`-> Config`) | Avoids heap allocation pressure; Rust moves values on the stack and applies Return Value Optimization (`RVO`). |
| Shared struct pointers mutated across goroutines | Single task owner + message passing (or scoped `Arc<RwLock<T>>` / atomics) | Prevents deadlocks, data races (`go test -race` gaps), and wrapping every field in `Arc<Mutex<T>>`. |
| `go func()` for network / Input-Output (`I/O`) work | `tokio::task::JoinSet` (draining `.join_next().await`) or awaited `JoinHandle` | Structured cooperative concurrency; never drop an unawaited `tokio::spawn` `JoinHandle` because detached tasks silently swallow `Result::Err` values and panics. |
| `go func()` for compute-heavy loops | `rayon::par_iter()` or `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` | Keeps processor-bound work off async executor worker threads so tail latency does not stall. |
| Unbounded or `chan T` pipelines | `tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(cap)` (bounded) / `oneshot` | Bounded capacity enforces explicit backpressure and prevents Out-Of-Memory (`OOM`) spikes under load. |
| `context.Context` cancellation & deadlines | Future drop cancellation, `tokio::time::timeout`, or `CancellationToken` | Dropping a Rust `Future` cancels work deterministically at `.await` points; use `CancellationToken` when graceful drain/flush is required before drop. |
| Implicit `interface{}` / `any` & type switches | Closed `enum` variants or generic `<T: Trait>` bounds | Moves dispatch and exhaustiveness checking to compile time (`dyn Trait` only for open plugin registries). |
| `if err != nil` + `defer f.Close()` | `#[must_use]` `Result<T, E>` with `?` + automatic `Drop` | Eliminates forgotten `defer` leaks, early-return nil-pointer bugs, and zero-value uninitialized structs (`Go` structs allow missing fields silently; Rust structs require every field at construction). |

### Key Go -> Rust Migration & `cgo` Interop Traps
* **Zero-Value Assumptions:** Go code frequently relies on zero-initialized structs (`var mu sync.Mutex`, nil slices behaving like empty slices on `len`/`append`, reading from a nil map returning zero). In Rust, model optional state explicitly (`Option<T>` / `Default` only where an empty default is domain-valid per `skills/mistake-proofing/SKILL.md`).
* **Blocking Inside `async fn`:** Never call `std::fs`, synchronous `reqwest::blocking`, `std::thread::sleep`, or `std::sync::Mutex` across `.await` points inside an async runtime (`clippy::await_holding_lock`); use `tokio::time::sleep` and async `I/O` or `spawn_blocking`.
* **Go `cgo` Bridge Constraints:** When bridging Go to a Rust `cdylib`/`staticlib` via `cgo`, never retain a Go pointer (`*T` or slice backing buffer) inside Rust after the `cgo` call returns (Go stacks move and Go's garbage collector forbids foreign retention of unpinned Go pointers), and batch records into contiguous byte buffers so `~100 ns` per-call `cgo` stack-switch overhead does not dominate hot loops.

---

## 2. Python -> Idiomatic Rust & `PyO3` Interop Matrix

| Python Pattern | Idiomatic Rust Replacement | Soundness & Architectural Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Untyped `dict[str, Any]` payloads | Typed `struct` + `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` at strict edges) | Parses unstructured boundary data once (`skills/mistake-proofing/SKILL.md` §3), eliminating downstream `KeyError` and `AttributeError` failures. |
| `T \| S \| None` (`Union` / `isinstance` chains) | `Option<DomainEnum>` with exhaustive `match` | Compiler rejects unhandled variants whenever the schema evolves. |
| Exception-driven flow control (`try / except`) | `Option<T>` / `Result<T, DomainError>` combinators | Makes recoverable failure modes explicit in signatures; map each `DomainError` variant `1`-to-`1` to the expected Python exception subclass (`PyKeyError`, `PyIndexError`, `PyTypeError`, `PyOSError`, `PyValueError`) at the outer `#[pyfunction]` / `#[pymethods]` seam. |
| List/dict comprehensions over large arrays | Chained iterators `.iter().filter(...).map(...).collect()` | Fuses transformations into a single pass without intermediate Python object allocations. |
| Compute-bound Python / NumPy hot loops | `PyO3` (`#[pyfunction]`) + `maturin` + Global Interpreter Lock (`GIL`) release (`py.allow_threads` / `py.detach`) | Releases the Python interpreter lock over pure-Rust slices (`&[f64]`, `numpy::PyReadonlyArray`) for true multi-core execution via `rayon`. |

### `PyO3` & `maturin` Hybrid Migration Rules
1. **Separate Pure Rust Core from Python Glue:** Place pure domain types, algorithms, and unit tests in a Rust core module (zero `pyo3` imports in core domain structs!) and keep a thin `py_bindings` adapter module converting `PyObject` / `Bound<'py, PyAny>` <-> domain Rust types once per call. Keep `panic = "unwind"` on `PyO3` extension wheels (`panic = "abort"` terminates the host Python interpreter instead of raising `PanicException`), and mark thread-affine `#[pyclass]` wrappers `#[pyclass(unsendable)]`.
2. **Release the `GIL` Safely & Respect Signals:** Before calling `py.allow_threads(|| ...)` (or `py.detach(|| ...)` in newer `PyO3` releases), extract owned data or borrowed raw slices that do not touch Python heap objects while unlocked, then re-acquire the `GIL` only to construct the final Python return object. In long loops that must hold the `GIL`, poll `py.check_signals()?` periodically so `Ctrl-C` (`KeyboardInterrupt`) is never blocked.
3. **Differential Equivalence Pinning (`pytest` + `cargo test`):** Keep the existing `pytest` suite running against the compiled `maturin develop` wheel alongside `cargo test` (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9). Pay special attention to Python arbitrary-precision `int` (which never overflows in Python but overflows `i64`/`u64` in Rust—use `i128`, `num-bigint`, or explicit overflow `PyOverflowError` checks!), negative slice indexing (`arr[-1]`), and `NaN` equality semantics.

# Security Review Skill

This skill enforces zero-trust security checks, defense-in-depth principles, and verifiable security boundaries.

## When to Activate

- Running a pre-deployment security checklist across secrets, HTTP headers, transport security, and cloud infrastructure
- User explicitly invokes `/security-review` or requests a `security review checklist`
- Verifying authentication, authorization, untrusted input/upload handling, API endpoints, credentials, or payment boundaries before release
- **Boundary Disambiguation:** For active code design of hard-to-misuse interfaces and compile-time state guards, use `mistake-proofing`. For read-only adversarial boundary audits with negative test generation, use `/audit --boundary` (`skills/audit/SKILL.md`).

## Context Hygiene & Think in Code

* **Computational Scanning:** When scanning for secrets, authorization boundaries, or injection vectors, do not pull source files one by one into conversation context. Execute targeted shell one-liners (`run_command` via ripgrep, Python, find) to extract only suspect lines.
* **Secret Protection:** Never emit `.env` files, SSH keys, or API tokens into command stdout or chat output.

## Subagent Orchestration

For critical security audits, authentication/authorization overhauls, or multi-tenant data boundaries, dispatch the `security-boundary-verifier` subagent via `invoke_subagent` to avoid polluting the main conversation context. The subagent inspects bounded file slices and authors reproducible negative boundary tests for the primary session to execute and verify.

---

## Security Verification Checklists

### 1. Secrets & Credentials Management
- [ ] No hardcoded API keys, secrets, private keys, or tokens in source code or git history.
- [ ] All credentials loaded strictly via environment variables or secret vaults.
- [ ] `.env*` files explicitly listed in `.gitignore`.
- [ ] Secret leaks scanned via computational check that reports LOCATIONS only, never values: `git grep -n -I -E -i "(api_key|secret|private_key|token)[[:space:]]*[:=]" | cut -d: -f1,2`.

### 2. Input Validation & Boundaries
- [ ] All inputs validated at system boundaries with strict typed schemas (e.g. Zod, Pydantic, Joi).
- [ ] Whitelist validation enforced over blacklists.
- [ ] File uploads validate magic bytes / MIME types, file extensions, and strict size caps.
- [ ] Path traversal prevented: reject `..`, unnormalized paths, or use `path.basename` / safe path resolution.

### 3. Injection Prevention (SQL / Command / Template)
- [ ] All SQL queries parameterized or executed through safe query builders/ORMs; zero raw string interpolation.
- [ ] Shell execution (`exec`, `spawn`, `subprocess`) uses argument arrays without `shell=True` / shell expansion.
- [ ] HTML sanitization enforced for user-provided markup (DOMPurify with restricted allowed tags/attributes).
- [ ] React / Vue default escaping preserved; avoid `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or `v-html` unless strictly sanitized.

### 4. Authentication & Authorization
- [ ] Authentication tokens stored in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies (avoid vulnerable `localStorage`).
- [ ] Authorization / permission checks performed on every private endpoint and server action; do not rely on client-side routing guards.
- [ ] Row Level Security (RLS) enabled on all multi-tenant database tables with strict user ownership policies.
- [ ] Passwords hashed using Argon2id or bcrypt with appropriate cost factors.

### 5. Transport & Header Security (CSP & CSRF)
- [ ] Content Security Policy (CSP) configured without `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'`.
- [ ] State-changing requests (POST/PUT/DELETE) protected by CSRF tokens or SameSite strict cookies.
- [ ] Security headers active: `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Strict-Transport-Security`.

### 6. Rate Limiting & DoS Protection
- [ ] Rate limiting active on authentication endpoints (login, register, password reset) and public APIs.
- [ ] Expensive endpoints (search, report generation, AI completion) protected by stricter per-user/IP caps.
- [ ] Payload size limits configured on incoming JSON/multipart requests.

### 7. Information Leakage & Error Handling
- [ ] User-facing error responses generic; stack traces, internal paths, and db errors logged strictly server-side.
- [ ] Logging utilities redact sensitive fields (`password`, `token`, `cardNumber`, `cvv`, `ssn`).

### 8. Dependency & Supply-Chain Security
- [ ] Dynamic execution tags (`@latest`, unpinned dependencies) forbidden.
- [ ] Lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `poetry.lock`) committed and verified.
- [ ] Vulnerability audit run via computational gate: `npm audit` or `pip-audit`.

---

## Pre-Deployment Verification Gate

1. **Static Secret Scan:** Run `git diff origin/main --name-only -G "(key|secret|token|password)[[:space:]]*[:=]"` to list files that add secret-like assignments (file names only; inspect them without echoing values).
2. **Cloud & Infrastructure:** For deployments, IAM, logging/monitoring or CI/CD changes, also apply the checklist in `references/cloud-infrastructure-security.md`.
3. **Endpoint Auth Audit:** Verify every exported route / controller implements explicit auth guard.
4. **Automated Security Tests:** Run integration tests verifying unauthorized access returns 401/403.
5. **Boundary & Result Requirement:** For every reported vulnerability, name the lower-trust principal, accepted input or action, crossed control boundary, and concrete owner-observable result; do not elevate a checklist preference or self-impact into a severity-ranked vulnerability.
6. **Source Visibility Discipline:** When external controls (reverse proxy, Web Application Firewall (WAF), Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy, or broker Access Control Lists (ACLs)) are absent from the repository, mark the item `[OPEN QUESTION]` with the exact missing deployment fact instead of assuming those controls exist or are missing.

# Cloud & Infrastructure Security Skill

This skill ensures cloud infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment configurations follow security best practices and comply with industry standards.

## When to Activate

- Deploying applications to cloud platforms (AWS, Vercel, Railway, Cloudflare)
- Configuring IAM roles and permissions
- Setting up CI/CD pipelines
- Implementing infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation)
- Configuring logging and monitoring
- Managing secrets in cloud environments
- Setting up CDN and edge security
- Implementing disaster recovery and backup strategies

## Cloud Security Checklist

### 1. IAM & Access Control

#### Principle of Least Privilege

```yaml
# PASS: CORRECT: Minimal permissions
iam_role:
  permissions:
    - s3:GetObject  # Only read access
    - s3:ListBucket
  resources:
    - arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*  # Specific bucket only

# FAIL: WRONG: Overly broad permissions
iam_role:
  permissions:
    - s3:*  # All S3 actions
  resources:
    - "*"  # All resources
```

#### Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

```bash
# ALWAYS enable MFA for root/admin accounts
aws iam enable-mfa-device \
  --user-name admin \
  --serial-number arn:aws:iam::123456789:mfa/admin \
  --authentication-code1 123456 \
  --authentication-code2 789012
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] No root account usage in production
- [ ] MFA enabled for all privileged accounts
- [ ] Service accounts use roles, not long-lived credentials
- [ ] IAM policies follow least privilege
- [ ] Regular access reviews conducted
- [ ] Unused credentials rotated or removed

### 2. Secrets Management

#### Cloud Secrets Managers

```typescript
// PASS: CORRECT: Use cloud secrets manager
import { SecretsManager } from '@aws-sdk/client-secrets-manager';

const client = new SecretsManager({ region: 'us-east-1' });
const secret = await client.getSecretValue({ SecretId: 'prod/api-key' });
const apiKey = JSON.parse(secret.SecretString).key;

// FAIL: WRONG: Hardcoded or in environment variables only
const apiKey = process.env.API_KEY; // Not rotated, not audited
```

#### Secrets Rotation

```bash
# Set up automatic rotation for database credentials
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret \
  --secret-id prod/db-password \
  --rotation-lambda-arn arn:aws:lambda:region:account:function:rotate \
  --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] All secrets stored in cloud secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vercel Secrets)
- [ ] Automatic rotation enabled for database credentials
- [ ] API keys rotated at least quarterly
- [ ] No secrets in code, logs, or error messages
- [ ] Audit logging enabled for secret access

### 3. Network Security

#### VPC and Firewall Configuration

```terraform
# PASS: CORRECT: Restricted security group
resource "aws_security_group" "app" {
  name = "app-sg"

  ingress {
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"]  # Internal VPC only
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]  # Only HTTPS outbound
  }
}

# FAIL: WRONG: Open to the internet
resource "aws_security_group" "bad" {
  ingress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 65535
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]  # All ports, all IPs!
  }
}
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] Database not publicly accessible
- [ ] SSH/RDP ports restricted to VPN/bastion only
- [ ] Security groups follow least privilege
- [ ] Network ACLs configured
- [ ] VPC flow logs enabled

### 4. Logging & Monitoring

#### CloudWatch/Logging Configuration

```typescript
// PASS: CORRECT: Comprehensive logging
import { CloudWatchLogsClient, CreateLogStreamCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-cloudwatch-logs';

const logSecurityEvent = async (event: SecurityEvent) => {
  await cloudwatch.putLogEvents({
    logGroupName: '/aws/security/events',
    logStreamName: 'authentication',
    logEvents: [{
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      message: JSON.stringify({
        type: event.type,
        userId: event.userId,
        ip: event.ip,
        result: event.result,
        // Never log sensitive data
      })
    }]
  });
};
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] CloudWatch/logging enabled for all services
- [ ] Failed authentication attempts logged
- [ ] Admin actions audited
- [ ] Log retention configured (90+ days for compliance)
- [ ] Alerts configured for suspicious activity
- [ ] Logs centralized and tamper-proof

### 5. CI/CD Pipeline Security

#### Secure Pipeline Configuration

```yaml
# PASS: CORRECT: Secure GitHub Actions workflow
name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read  # Minimal permissions

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Scan for secrets
      - name: Secret scanning
        uses: trufflesecurity/trufflehog@main

      # Dependency audit
      - name: Audit dependencies
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high

      # Use OIDC, not long-lived tokens
      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/GitHubActionsRole
          aws-region: us-east-1
```

#### Supply Chain Security

```json
// package.json - Use lock files and integrity checks
{
  "scripts": {
    "install": "npm ci",  // Use ci for reproducible builds
    "audit": "npm audit --audit-level=moderate",
    "check": "npm outdated"
  }
}
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] OIDC used instead of long-lived credentials
- [ ] Secrets scanning in pipeline
- [ ] Dependency vulnerability scanning
- [ ] Container image scanning (if applicable)
- [ ] Branch protection rules enforced
- [ ] Code review required before merge
- [ ] Signed commits enforced

### 6. Cloudflare & CDN Security

#### Cloudflare Security Configuration

```typescript
// PASS: CORRECT: Cloudflare Workers with security headers
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    const response = await fetch(request);

    // Add security headers
    const headers = new Headers(response.headers);
    headers.set('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY');
    headers.set('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff');
    headers.set('Referrer-Policy', 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin');
    headers.set('Permissions-Policy', 'geolocation=(), microphone=()');

    return new Response(response.body, {
      status: response.status,
      headers
    });
  }
};
```

#### WAF Rules

```bash
# Enable Cloudflare WAF managed rules
# - OWASP Core Ruleset
# - Cloudflare Managed Ruleset
# - Rate limiting rules
# - Bot protection
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] WAF enabled with OWASP rules
- [ ] Rate limiting configured
- [ ] Bot protection active
- [ ] DDoS protection enabled
- [ ] Security headers configured
- [ ] SSL/TLS strict mode enabled

### 7. Backup & Disaster Recovery

#### Automated Backups

```terraform
# PASS: CORRECT: Automated RDS backups
resource "aws_db_instance" "main" {
  allocated_storage     = 20
  engine               = "postgres"

  backup_retention_period = 30  # 30 days retention
  backup_window          = "03:00-04:00"
  maintenance_window     = "mon:04:00-mon:05:00"

  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["postgresql"]

  deletion_protection = true  # Prevent accidental deletion
}
```

#### Verification Steps

- [ ] Automated daily backups configured
- [ ] Backup retention meets compliance requirements
- [ ] Point-in-time recovery enabled
- [ ] Backup testing performed quarterly
- [ ] Disaster recovery plan documented
- [ ] RPO and RTO defined and tested

## Pre-Deployment Cloud Security Checklist

Before ANY production cloud deployment:

- [ ] **IAM**: Root account not used, MFA enabled, least privilege policies
- [ ] **Secrets**: All secrets in cloud secrets manager with rotation
- [ ] **Network**: Security groups restricted, no public databases
- [ ] **Logging**: CloudWatch/logging enabled with retention
- [ ] **Monitoring**: Alerts configured for anomalies
- [ ] **CI/CD**: OIDC auth, secrets scanning, dependency audits
- [ ] **CDN/WAF**: Cloudflare WAF enabled with OWASP rules
- [ ] **Encryption**: Data encrypted at rest and in transit
- [ ] **Backups**: Automated backups with tested recovery
- [ ] **Compliance**: GDPR/HIPAA requirements met (if applicable)
- [ ] **Documentation**: Infrastructure documented, runbooks created
- [ ] **Incident Response**: Security incident plan in place

## Common Cloud Security Misconfigurations

### S3 Bucket Exposure

```bash
# FAIL: WRONG: Public bucket
aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket my-bucket --acl public-read

# PASS: CORRECT: Private bucket with specific access
aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket my-bucket --acl private
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket my-bucket --policy file://policy.json
```

### RDS Public Access

```terraform
# FAIL: WRONG
resource "aws_db_instance" "bad" {
  publicly_accessible = true  # NEVER do this!
}

# PASS: CORRECT
resource "aws_db_instance" "good" {
  publicly_accessible = false
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.db.id]
}
```

## Resources

- [AWS Security Best Practices](https://aws.amazon.com/security/best-practices/)
- [CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/amazon_web_services)
- [Cloudflare Security Documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/security/)
- [OWASP Cloud Security](https://owasp.org/www-project-cloud-security/)
- [Terraform Security Best Practices](https://www.terraform.io/docs/cloud/guides/recommended-practices/)

**Remember**: Cloud misconfigurations are the leading cause of data breaches. A single exposed S3 bucket or overly permissive IAM policy can compromise your entire infrastructure. Always follow the principle of least privilege and defense in depth.

# silk-design — Kinetic Interface and Motion Engineering Toolkit

This skill equips web interfaces with buttery smooth, physics-based motion, fluid typography, and centrally orchestrated design tokens modeled after modern showcase experiences.

---

## 1. Architectural Hierarchy and Constitutional Bridge

This skill is **not an independent design system or style arbiter**. It operates strictly within the three-tier design hierarchy:

1. **`DESIGN.md` (Identity & Soul):** Dictates project identity, color tokens, typography, and dials.
2. **`antislop` (Filter & Delivery Gate):** Prevents gratuitous trend accumulation, fake content, accessibility violations, and visual bloat.
3. **`silk-design` (Kinetic Armory):** Implements the antislop tenet: *"Removing slop does not make a design great; vitality must be added purposefully"* via verified physics and animation formulas.

### Invocation and Scope Rules

* **Allowed Scenarios:**
  * The user explicitly requests a showcase, landing page, marketing site, portfolio, or creative experience (`/silk-design`, `silk-design`, `motion 3`, "fluid kinetic motion").
  * The project's local `DESIGN.md` declares the motion dial as **`MOTION 3`**.
* **STRICTLY Prohibited Scenarios:**
  * Standard engineering dashboards, administrative consoles, CRUD interfaces, and data tables.
  * Projects declaring **`MOTION 1`** (`0ms` / static, instantaneous state changes) or **`MOTION 2`** (`150ms–200ms` functional micro-interactions; Lenis and scroll animations are barred).

---

## 2. Antislop Safety Boundaries (Mandatory Invariants)

Every technique in `silk-design` must pass the `antislop` delivery gate:

1. **Accessibility and Motion Preference (`prefers-reduced-motion` - R-19):**
   * Always emit client-side `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` CSS rules and `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` JavaScript guards so if the host system enables "reduce motion", Lenis smooth-scrolling, parallax, and GSAP ScrollTrigger are disabled entirely or collapsed to instant zero-duration transitions (`duration: 0`, `MOTION 1`).
2. **Glassmorphism Discipline (R-10):**
   * Do not apply `.card { backdrop-filter: blur(8px); }` indiscriminately across cards. Reserve blur solely for sticky navigation bars, modals, or drawers where visible underlay content provides spatial depth.
3. **Contrast and Glow Limits (R-13, R-25):**
   * Glow effects (`BorderGlow`, `neon`) must never compromise text legibility. All typography must maintain at least **WCAG AA 4.5:1** contrast against backgrounds.
4. **Honest Content (R-17, R-18, R-38):**
   * Reference compositions (`references/templates.md`) are wireframe skeletons only. Do not copy fake testimonial quotes, fabricated logos, or artificial counters into production. If real data is unavailable, omit those sections.

---

## 3. Non-Negotiable Engineering Foundation

The baseline skeleton for kinetic showcase experiences:

### 1. Root-Level Lenis Smooth Scrolling
Wrap the application root once; **never** use CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth`:
```tsx
import { ReactLenis } from 'lenis/react'
<ReactLenis root>{app}</ReactLenis>
```
Trigger in-page anchor navigation via `useLenis().scrollTo(el)` (see `assets/useButtonClick.ts`).

### 2. Overscroll Bounce Prevention and Thin Scrollbar
Global CSS rules in `assets/foundation.css`:
```css
html, body { overscroll-behavior: none; }
* { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3) transparent; }
```

### 3. Token Architecture and Single Radius Knob (`--radius`)
Nine CSS variables and a single `--radius` knob govern site-wide color and corner radiuses (Tailwind v4 `@theme inline`). The hex values below are illustrative `MOTION 3` showcase defaults; always defer to the active project's `DESIGN.md` tokens (e.g., `#09090B` / `#18181B`) unless an explicit showcase palette override is declared:
```css
:root {
  --background: #0a0a0a;
  --card: #1a1a1a;
  --foreground: #eeeded;
  --primary-cta: #00FFAB;
  --primary-cta-text: #000000;
  --secondary-cta: #1a1a1a;
  --secondary-cta-text: #ffffffe6;
  --accent: #8a8a8a;
  --background-accent: #00d5c7;
  --radius: 0.75rem; /* Single knob: lg, md, sm derive from here */
}

@theme inline {
  --color-background: var(--background);
  --color-card: var(--card);
  --color-foreground: var(--foreground);
  --color-primary-cta: var(--primary-cta);
  --color-primary-cta-text: var(--primary-cta-text);
  --color-secondary-cta: var(--secondary-cta);
  --color-secondary-cta-text: var(--secondary-cta-text);
  --color-accent: var(--accent);
  --color-background-accent: var(--background-accent);
  --radius-lg: var(--radius);
  --radius-md: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  --radius-sm: calc(var(--radius) - 4px);
}
```

### 4. Fluid Typography
Replace rigid pixel breakpoints with `clamp(min, vw + rem, max)` scalers (minimum `0.75rem` / `12px` floor per `antislop` R-06). Text scales smoothly with viewport width and browser zoom without causing mobile horizontal overflow:
```css
--text-lg:  clamp(1rem, 1vw + 0.65rem, 1.125rem);
--text-4xl: clamp(1.5rem, 2vw + 0.9rem, 2.25rem);
--text-6xl: clamp(2.25rem, 3.3vw + 1.1rem, 3.3rem);
--text-9xl: clamp(3.25rem, 7vw + 1.5rem, 7rem);
```

### 5. Standard Entrance Reveal Choreography
Uniform reveal rhythm across blocks (React `motion/react` or zero-build `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js` `[data-silk-reveal]` / `[data-silk-words]`):
```tsx
initial="hidden" whileInView="visible"
viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-20%" }}
transition={{ duration: 0.6, ease: "easeOut" }} // Text staggerChildren: 0.04
```
Available components: `assets/ScrollReveal.tsx` (blocks), `assets/TextAnimation.tsx` (word-by-word titles), and `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js` (`initSilkKinetic()` for zero-build HTML/Astro/Vanilla JS).

---

## 4. Toolkit and Asset Directory

Consult the reference library when needed:
* **Entrances & Text Effects:** Word-by-word animated headers, blur-to-sharp transitions. → `references/effects.md`, `assets/{TextAnimation,ScrollReveal}.tsx`, `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js`
* **Scroll-Driven Effects:** Parallax (`useScroll`/`useTransform` or native CSS `animation-timeline: view()`), scrubbed video, pinned sections, revealed footers. → `references/effects.md`, `assets/{HeroVideoScroll,AboutTextFill,FooterBrandReveal}.tsx`
* **Cursor & Pointer Interactions:** Magnetic buttons (spring `150/15` or `[data-silk-magnetic]`), pointer-following border glows (`[data-silk-border-glow]`), draggable tags. → `references/effects.md`, `assets/{ButtonMagnetic,BorderGlow,HoverPattern}.tsx`, `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js`
* **Marquees:** Infinite CSS marquee with edge gradient masks. → `references/effects.md`, `assets/{animations,masks}.css`
* **Page Transitions:** Fullscreen curtain overlay, DrawSVG spiral transitions, or native `View Transitions API` (`runSilkViewTransition`). → `references/effects.md`, `assets/{NavbarFullscreen,PageTransitionSwirl}.tsx`, `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js`
* **10 Style Skins:** Ten pre-built styling palettes in `references/design-system.md` (minimal, elegant, soft, bold, glass, neon, gradient, metallic, shadow, elevated). Switch skins by swapping `.card` and `.primary-button` CSS definitions (subject to Section 2: `glass` blur is restricted to sticky navbars/modals/drawers per R-10, and `neon` glow is restricted to a single primary focal CTA per R-13).
* **23 Reference Compositions:** Production-ready color palettes, font pairings, and section rhythms in `references/templates.md`.

---

## 5. Technology Stack (Dual-Track Runtime)

 Domain scope remains strictly locked to **`MODE: EDITORIAL` (`MOTION 3`)** showcase, landing, portfolio, and interactive narrative pages (`MODE: UTILITY` dashboards and CRUD tables remain prohibited). Within that editorial scope, two first-class runtime tracks are supported:

1. **Track A — Component Framework Stack (React / Next.js):**
   * **Core:** React + Vite (or Next.js) + Tailwind v4 + `assets/*.tsx`
   * **Kinetic Libraries:** `motion` (`motion/react`), `gsap` + `@gsap/react` (ScrollTrigger, Draggable, DrawSVGPlugin), and `lenis` (`lenis/react`).
2. **Track B — Zero-Build Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, Astro & Static Runtime:**
   * **Core:** `assets/foundation.css` + `assets/animations.css` + `assets/masks.css` + `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js` (`initSilkKinetic()` and `runSilkViewTransition()`).
   * **Native Browser Primitives:** CSS `clamp()` fluid typography, `IntersectionObserver` (`-20%` root margin, `once: true`) word/block reveals, CSS Scroll-Driven Animations (`animation-timeline: view()`), `document.startViewTransition` curtain wipes, and rAF-throttled `[data-silk-magnetic]` / `[data-silk-border-glow]` pointer physics — all automatically guarded by `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` (`antislop` R-19).

# Animated backgrounds — 13 of them Ambient motion behind content. Subtle by design (opacities 5–20%) — they add life without competing. Three are shipped in `assets/`; all 13 follow one pattern, so you can build any from the recipe. ## The shared pattern (every background) ```tsx const Background = ({ position }: { position: "fixed" | "absolute" }) => (
{/* low-opacity token-colored layers, animated via a keyframe class */}
); ``` - `-z-10` + `pointer-events-none` → sits behind content, never intercepts clicks. - `position="fixed"` for a whole-page ambient; `"absolute"` to scope it to one section (the mask fades it in/out at the section's top/bottom so it doesn't hard-edge). - Colors come from tokens (`bg-background-accent/15`, `bg-primary-cta`) so it recolors with the theme. - Motion comes from the keyframes in `assets/animations.css` — no JS. ## The catalog | background | look | how it's built | driven by | |---|---|---|---| | **Aurora** ✅ | soft diagonal color veils, blurred | 5 rotated `rounded-[100%]` blobs at `bg-background-accent/10–20` + `backdrop-blur-3xl` | static (or `@keyframes aurora` bg-position drift) | | **GradientBars** ✅ | faint vertical light bars L & R | two rows of `flex-1` bars, `opacity-0.075`, `bg-[linear-gradient(90deg,var(--color-primary-cta),transparent)]`, mask-faded | static | | **Noise** ✅ | film-grain texture | tiled `noise.webp` at `mix-blend-overlay opacity-10 bg-size-[512px]` | static | | **NoiseGradient** | grain + a color wash | Noise layer over a radial/linear token gradient | static | | **LightRaysCenter** | rays pulsing from center | angled thin gradient slivers rotated around center | `@keyframes ray-pulse` (opacity 0↔`--ray-opacity`) | | **LightRaysCorner** | rays from a corner | same, anchored to a corner | `@keyframes rotated-ray-pulse` | | **FloatingGradient** | slow-drifting color blobs | 2–3 blurred radial blobs | `floating-move-in-circle / -vertical / -horizontal` | | **CornerGlow** | soft glow bleeding from a corner | one large blurred radial at low opacity | static / slow pulse | | **HorizonGlow** | glowing horizon band | wide blurred gradient bar low on the section | static | | **RadialGradient** | vignette-ish center glow | single `radial-gradient` token layer | static | | **GridLines** | faint technical grid | repeating-linear-gradient grid at low opacity | static | | **ColumnWave** | columns lighting up in sequence | grid of columns | `@keyframes cell-wave-pulse` (staggered opacity) | | **Grid dots** | dotted grid | `radial-gradient` dot pattern, low opacity | static | ✅ = shipped in `assets/`. The rest: build from the pattern above + the named keyframe (all keyframes are already in `assets/animations.css`). Aurora, Noise, and a subtle RadialGradient are the safest defaults for most sites. ## Choosing one - Dark, techy, premium → Aurora, LightRays, GradientBars. - Warm / editorial / product → Noise or NoiseGradient (barely-there grain reads as "print quality"). - Clean SaaS → GridLines or Grid dots + a CornerGlow. - **One per page, low opacity.** Two competing animated backgrounds is noise, not polish.

# Composition — assembling a page How the sites are built above the effect level: the page skeleton, the section contract every section follows, and the authoring rules that keep 100 sections feeling like one system. ## Page skeleton (assembly order) ```tsx {/* smooth scroll — once, at the top */} {/* optional: behind everything */}
…pricing · testimonials · faq · cta…
``` - Each section gets an `id` (for anchor-scroll via `useButtonClick`/Lenis) + a `data-section` name. - Sections take **flat content props** (`tag`, `title`, `description`, `primaryButton:{text,href}`, `items[]`, `imageSrc`/`videoSrc`, `textAnimation`) — no nested config objects. ## The section contract Every section's inner content is centered in a content-width wrapper and animates in: ```tsx
{/* — canonical header — */}
{tag}
{/* — body — */} {/* grid or carousel of cards */}
``` This exact header pattern repeats across ~90% of sections — that repetition is what makes the sites feel coherent. Secondary button always `animationDelay={0.1}` so it trails the primary. ## Responsive padding & gap scale (use verbatim) - Card padding: `p-6 xl:p-7 2xl:p-8` - Grid/flex gaps: `gap-4 xl:gap-5 2xl:gap-6` - Section vertical rhythm: `py-20` (or `py-60` for a dramatic standalone moment). - Titles are `font-semibold` (not medium); big numbers/stats `text-8xl`–`text-9xl font-semibold`. ## Grid-or-carousel rule For a row of cards: **≤3 items → CSS grid; >3 → carousel** (Embla, `dragFree: true`, `cursor-grab`, a `translate3d` progress bar + chevrons). Keeps small sets clean and large sets swipeable instead of cramped. Edge case: exactly 4 items → grid on `2xl:` screens, carousel below (both rendered, toggled by breakpoint). ## Bento live widgets — what goes in the cells A bento grid earns its keep when 2–3 cells *move*. The kit's widget menu (each is a self-contained `h-full` component dropped into a card cell; recipes in effects.md where noted): - **animated-bar-chart** — bars at preset heights; one "active" bar cycles every 3s (`primary-button` overlay fades in); hover swaps ALL bars to alternate heights (`transition-all duration-500`). Bottom-fade mask so it melts into the card. - **chat-marquee** — fake live chat: alternating user/AI bubbles in a vertical marquee (`mask-fade-y`) over a static input row. Sells "AI product" instantly. - **orbiting-icons** — center icon + icons on `animation: orbit 12s linear infinite` (keyframe in `animations.css`, per-icon `--initial-position: (360/n)*i deg`), concentric border rings at decreasing opacity, all inside `perspective: 2000px` + `rotateY(20deg) rotateX(20deg) rotateZ(-20deg)` for the 3D look, edge-masked with intersecting X+Y fades. - **tilted-stack-cards** — three cards in one grid area (`[grid-template-areas:'stack']`), all `-skew-y-[8deg]`, offset by translates; hover nudges each apart (`duration-500`). - **media-stack** — hover fan-out photo stack (effects.md). - **checklist-timeline** — staged hover scene with utility delays (effects.md). - **info-card-marquee / icon-text-marquee** — vertical tickers of stat/icon rows, `mask-fade-y`. Pattern: widgets are pure CSS/keyframe motion (no scroll listeners), token-colored, and masked at their edges so they read as *inside* the card, not pasted on. ## Navbar archetypes `NavbarInline` (logo + links + CTA in a bar) · `NavbarCentered` (links centered) · `NavbarFloating` (detached pill, `top-5`, card bg) · `NavbarFloatingLogo` (floating logo only) · `NavbarDropdown` (inline + hover panels) · `NavbarCenteredOverlay` (transparent over hero) · `NavbarFullscreen` (hamburger → fullscreen curtain menu — the premium option; recipe in effects.md + `assets/NavbarFullscreen.tsx`) · `NavbarFullscreenStatic` (same, always hamburger). Pick ONE; floating pill for light/product sites, fullscreen curtain for editorial/luxury/portfolio. ## Section archetype menu (what to reach for) - **Hero** — split (text + media), billboard (full-bleed image + overlay), scroll-scrubbed video (`assets/HeroVideoScroll.tsx`), pinned card-stack, floating-cards, tilted carousel, **brand wordmark** (giant name spanning full width via `assets/AutoFillText.tsx`), sticker-flip (draggable stickers + 3D flip card — effects.md), stack-to-grid work reel (effects.md). - **Features** — icon/media cards, **bento grid** (mixed-size cards with live mini-widgets — see "Bento live widgets" above), **pinned sticky cards** (scrub), 3D flip cards, alternating split, comparison table, filterable grid, image **reveal cards** (hover panel + expanding description). - **About / editorial** — reading word-fill (`assets/AboutTextFill.tsx`), two-layer parallax, cursor image-trail (`assets/AboutCursorTrail.tsx`), text+media split. - **Testimonials** — dual-row horizontal marquee, vertical column marquee, avatar/quote/rating cards. - **Pricing** — highlighted plan (ribbon), centered/simple/split/layered cards. - **FAQ** — single-open accordion (`AnimatePresence`, `height: 0 → auto`, `opacity 0→1`, `duration 0.3`, Plus-icon `rotate-45` on open), two-column, tabbed. - **Metrics** — big-number stat cards. **Social proof** — single-row logo/name marquee. - **CTA / contact** — centered CTA, split form (+ parallax), contact bar. - **Footer** — reveal-from-behind (`assets/FooterBrandReveal.tsx`), brand wordmark, simple columns. ## Authoring rules (why 100 sections still feel like one system) Follow these when you write sections: - **Flat > nested, explicit > implicit.** One file per section, content variables at the top. Don't split a section into sub-components. Keep sections under ~100 lines, UI primitives under ~50. - **Single default export** per file. No compound components, no `className` prop drilling — edit classes in-file. - **Framer Motion `whileInView` for element animation; GSAP only for scroll-scrub / pin / timeline work** (scrubbed video, cursor trail, pinned stacks). Don't reach for GSAP when a `whileInView` does it. - **Class order:** layout → spacing → sizing → typography → colors → effects. (Consistent, greppable.) - Media from a CDN, never committed. `object-cover` + a fixed `aspect-*` box so images never jump. - One animated background per page, low opacity. One button hover-personality per site.
