# Effects catalog — exact configs Every config below is a tuned default. The numbers carry the feel — use them as given unless you have a reason not to. Group: entrance · scroll-driven · cursor/pointer · hover · marquees/carousels · navigation & page transitions · loaders. --- ## Entrance reveals ### Word-stagger heading — `assets/TextAnimation.tsx` Splits text on spaces, reveals each word with a stagger. The signature heading animation. - Container: `whileInView`, `viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-20%" }}`, `transition={{ staggerChildren: 0.04 }}`. - Per word: `transition={{ duration: 0.6, ease }}`. - Variants: `slide-up` (`y: "50%"→0`, ease `[0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94]`), `fade-blur` (`blur(10px)→none`, ease `[0.45, 0, 0.55, 1]`), `fade`. - Optional gradient text-clip fills in ~700ms after the reveal (`from-foreground to-primary-cta bg-clip-text text-transparent`). ### Block reveal — `assets/ScrollReveal.tsx` Wrap any block; it fades/slides in once when scrolled into view. - `whileInView`, `viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-20%" }}`, `transition={{ duration: 0.6, delay, ease: "easeOut" }}`. - `slide-up` = `y: 20→0`. Stagger siblings by passing increasing `delay` (0, 0.1, 0.2…). **The margin `-20%` matters:** it fires the reveal when the element is 20% into the viewport, not at the very edge — so content is already moving before the user reaches it. `once: true` = never re-hide. --- ## Scroll-driven effects ### Parallax (two-layer depth) — `motion/react` Layers move at different rates as the section scrolls past. Principle: map scroll progress → transform. ```tsx const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({ target: ref, offset: ["start end", "end start"] }); const yFront = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [120, -120]); // front layer const yBack = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [-60, 60]); // back layer const scale = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [1, 1.15]); // subtle zoom // … style={{ y: yBack, scale }} ``` ### Reading word-fill — `assets/AboutTextFill.tsx` Big paragraph where each word brightens `0.15 → 1` opacity as you scroll through it (premium editorial feel). - `useScroll({ target, offset: ["start 0.8", "start 0.2"] })`. - Per word `i` of `n`: `useTransform(scrollYProgress, [i/n, (i+1)/n], [0.15, 1])`. ### Scroll-scrubbed video — `assets/HeroVideoScroll.tsx` (GSAP) Video scrubs frame-by-frame as you scroll — feels like a controlled cinematic. The showstopper hero. - Outer `h-[300vh]`, inner `sticky top-0 h-svh`. - `ScrollTrigger.create({ trigger, start: "top top", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5, onUpdate: self => { video.currentTime = video.duration * self.progress } })`. - Video: `muted playsInline preload="auto"`. Wait for `canplaythrough` (8s fallback) before wiring. - Includes a clip-path loader (see Loaders) and content entrance `opacity:0,y:30 → dur 0.8, delay 0.2/0.4, ease [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]`. ### Pinned + scrubbed card stack — GSAP ScrollTrigger Section holds still while inner cards animate on scroll. Principle: tall section + `sticky` inner + scrub. - Section height `= items.length * 100vh`; inner `sticky top-0 h-screen`. - Per card: `gsap.fromTo(card, { xPercent: ±225, rotation: ±45 }, { xPercent: 0, rotation: ±10, scrollTrigger: { trigger, start: "top bottom", end: "top top", scrub: 1 } })`. - Or fade a stack out one-by-one: `sticky top-[12.5vh] h-[75vh]`, scrub `opacity → 0`, `ease: "none"`. ### Hero exit-parallax (scroll-away) The hero's media drifts down and zooms as you scroll *off* it — the "leave-behind" counterpart to section parallax. Used by several kit heroes (`HeroExpand`, `HeroOverlayParallax`): ```tsx const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({ target: heroRef, offset: ["start start", "end start"] }); const y = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], ["0px", "150px"]); const scale = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [1, 1.1]); // ``` Variant — **floating gutter cards**: small cards absolutely positioned in the content-width gutter (`left-[calc((100vw-var(--width-content-width))/2)]`) with `y: "0%" → "-100%"` / `"-75%"` on the same offset, so they float up past the hero at different rates. ### Tilt-flatten billboard — 3D perspective on scroll Hero media starts tilted back in 3D and flattens as it scrolls into view (the "container scroll" look). Wrapper gets Tailwind `perspective-distant`; the media card: ```tsx const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({ target: containerRef }); const rotate = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [20, 0]); // rotateX const scale = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [1.05, 1]); // ``` Mobile: skip the JS, ship a static `rotate-x-20`. ### Stack-to-grid scroll (FLIP-style) — GSAP Cards start stacked/fanned inside the hero, then scrub back into their natural grid slots in the next section as you scroll (`HeroWorkScrollStack`, the portfolio showcase). The trick: **measure, then transform** — cards live in their final grid position in the DOM; compute the delta to the hero placeholder and set it as the initial transform. - `yOffset = placeholderCenterY - cardCenterY` (from `getBoundingClientRect`), plus per-card `x` offsets, `rotation: [-5, 0, 5]`, `scale: ~1.3`, staggered `zIndex`. - Desktop: one timeline, `scrollTrigger: { trigger: wrapper, start: "top top", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 1 }`, each card `tl.to(card, { x: 0, y: 0, rotation: 0, scale: 1 }, 0)`. - Mobile: same `gsap.set`, but a plain tween with `scrollTrigger: { start: "top 35%", toggleActions: "play none none reverse" }`. - Always `gsap.set(card, { willChange: "transform", force3D: true })` first. ### Footer reveal-from-behind — `assets/FooterBrandReveal.tsx` Page content scrolls up like a sheet, uncovering a fixed footer sitting underneath. No JS scroll math. - Outer `section`: `position: relative`, `clipPath: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%)` (creates a clip context), height set to the footer's measured height (ResizeObserver). - Inner footer: `position: fixed; bottom: 0`. Because the section clips, the footer only shows as page scrolls past. Pair with a giant auto-fitting wordmark (`AutoFillText`, canvas-measured to span full width). --- ## Cursor & pointer ### Magnetic button — `assets/ButtonMagnetic.tsx` Button leans toward the cursor when hovered. Subtle, expensive-feeling. - `useSpring(useMotionValue(0), { stiffness: 150, damping: 15 })` for x and y. - On mousemove: `offset = (cursor - center) * 0.15`; on leave: reset to 0. - **Disabled below 768px** (`window.innerWidth < 768`) — no cursor on touch. ### Cursor image-trail — `assets/AboutCursorTrail.tsx` (GSAP, the showpiece) Moving the cursor drops a trail of images that fade out — the "move your cursor!" moment. - `gsap.matchMedia()`: desktop = mousemove, mobile = scroll-driven random placement. - Fires when the cursor moves more than `window.innerWidth / 15` since the last drop. - Drop: `gsap.set(img, { x, y, zIndex, force3D })` then `fromTo(img, { autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.8 }, { autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.2, overwrite: true })`. - Idle fade after 350ms: `gsap.to(img, { autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.2, duration: 0.8, ease: "expo.out" })`. - Gated by `ScrollTrigger.create({ start: "top bottom", end: "bottom top", onEnter/onLeave })` so it only runs while on screen. Always `mm.revert()` in cleanup. ### Pointer-tracked border glow — `assets/BorderGlow.tsx` A conic-gradient segment lights up the card's border and rotates toward the cursor. The premium "lit edge" for feature cards (drop inside any `relative rounded` card). - CSS vars drive it: `--start` (angle), `--active` (0/1), `--spread: 40`, `--border-width: 1.5px`. - On pointermove (rAF-throttled, one listener on `body`): activate when cursor is within `proximity: 64px` of the card rect; compute `targetAngle = atan2(y-cy, x-cx) + 90°`, then animate `--start` there with motion's `animate(current, target, { duration: 2, ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] })` (shortest-path via `((diff+180)%360)-180`). - The visible ring is an `::after` with a token gradient, masked to a conic slice: `mask: linear-gradient(#0000,#0000), conic-gradient(from calc((var(--start)-var(--spread))*1deg), transparent, #fff, transparent …)` + `[mask-clip:padding-box,border-box]` + `mask-intersect` — only the border area shows, only in the slice. ### Cursor-mask character pattern — `assets/HoverPattern.tsx` Hovering a card reveals a drifting field of random characters + an accent gradient through a radial mask that follows the cursor — the "encrypted" hover. - `useMotionValue` x/y + `useMotionTemplate` mask: `radial-gradient(250px at ${x}px ${y}px, white, transparent)`. - Three stacked layers, all `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-*`: a faint `linear-gradient(var(--foreground), transparent)` wash (25%), an accent gradient + `backdrop-blur-xl` (masked), and a `mix-blend-overlay` layer with 1500 random chars in `font-mono text-xs` (masked; regenerate chars on each mousemove). - Mobile: pin the mask to center at 110px, always-on, no listeners. ### Draggable stickers — GSAP Draggable Scattered sticker images the user can fling around the hero (`HeroStickerFlip`, the playful showcase). - Entrance: `gsap.fromTo(el, { autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.5, y: 30 }, { autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.6, delay: 0.8 + i * 0.08, ease: "back.out(2)" })`. - `Draggable.create(el, { type: "x,y", bounds: container, dragResistance: 0.1 })`; onPress `scale: 1.15, rotation: (Math.random()-0.5)*20, ease: "power2.out"`; onRelease `scale: 1, rotation: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: "back.out(3)"` — pick up, wiggle, snap back. - Scatter via a positions table (`top/left/right/bottom %` + `rotate ±4–14deg`), `drop-shadow-lg`, `cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing`. Register `gsap/Draggable`; wrap in `gsap.context`, revert on cleanup. --- ## Hover micro-interactions — 12 button variants All share the entrance `initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }} whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} viewport={{ once: true }} transition={{ duration: 0.6, ease: "easeOut" }}`. Pick per site for a consistent hover personality: - **expand** — a fill panel slides in from the left on hover (`-translate-x-full → translate-x-0`, `duration-500 ease-out`), text color swaps primary↔secondary. The default; safe and classy. - **magnetic** — leans toward cursor (above). - **slide / shift** — label + arrow slide together on hover. - **stagger** — each character rolls up (`translateY(-1.25em)` with a `textShadow: 0 1.25em currentColor` trick to fake a second copy), `transitionDelay: index * 0.01`. - **bounce / elastic / bubble / flip / pill / arrow** — spring/rotate/scale flourishes on the icon or label. Principle for any of them: a `group` wrapper + `transition` on a child that reacts to `group-hover:`. Keep durations 300–500ms and easings gentle; the point is polish, not spectacle. ## Hover micro-interactions — beyond buttons ### The grid-fr expand trick (animate to `auto` size, pure CSS) CSS can't transition `width/height: auto` — but it CAN transition grid fractions. Wrap the content: ```html
…content…
``` Same for height: `grid-rows-[0fr] group-hover:grid-rows-[1fr]`. The kit uses it for a button that grows a second avatar on hover, and for card descriptions that expand below the title. Pair the inner content with its own `-translate-x-3 group-hover:translate-x-0` + opacity for a directional feel. ### Image reveal card (`FeaturesRevealCards`) Full-bleed image card; on hover a panel slides up behind the caption and the description expands: - Frosted scrim: bottom strip `h-2/5 backdrop-blur-xl` masked with `mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, black 60%)` — blur fades in, no hard edge. - Panel: `absolute inset-0 -z-10 card rounded translate-y-full opacity-0 → group-hover:translate-y-0 opacity-100`, `duration-400 ease-out`. - Description: the grid-rows-fr trick above. Title swaps `text-white → text-foreground`. ### 3D flip card (Tailwind v4 utilities, no JS beyond a toggle) ```tsx
setFlipped(!flipped)}>
…front…
…back…
``` Front corner: `Plus` icon; back: same icon `rotate-45` (= ×). For a big hero flip use hover to toggle and a bouncy `duration-1200 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.22,0.68,0,1.2)]` — the overshoot sells it. ### Hover fan-out stack (`MediaStack`) Three overlapping media cards fanned `±rotate-8` + translate; on `group-hover` each pushes further out (`rotate-12`, larger translate), `duration-500`. Cheap depth, great in bento cells. ### Staged hover scene (`ChecklistTimeline`) A hover can play a little *sequence* with nothing but utility delays: checkmarks pop in at `delay-150/-[350ms]/-[550ms]` (`opacity-0 scale-75 → 100`), labels fade behind each (`delay-200/-[400ms]/-[600ms]`), a loader icon spins (`group-hover:rotate-360 duration-1000`), and at `delay-900` the footer dots swap to a "completed" label. One `group`, zero JS. --- ## Marquees & carousels — `assets/animations.css` + `assets/masks.css` Infinite horizontal/vertical scroll (logos, testimonials, tags). Pure CSS, no JS. - Duplicate the item array **4×** inside an `overflow-hidden` track, apply `.animate-marquee-horizontal`. - Keyframe translates `0 → -50%` (that's why you duplicate — the second copy fills the gap seamlessly). - Feather both ends with `.mask-fade-x` so items don't hard-cut at the edges. - Speeds: horizontal default `15s`, vertical `40s`; override per-row via inline `style={{ animationDuration: "30s" }}`. Run two rows in opposite directions (`-reverse` variant) for a richer feel. - The marquee is also a **widget chassis**: fake live chat (alternating bubbles in a card, marquee-vertical + `mask-fade-y` + a static input row below), info/stat tickers, before/after card streams (slow, `60s`). ### Deck carousel (`TiltedCarousel`) — the 3D-ish auto-rotating deck Five slots `[-2,-1,0,1,2]`, item index = `(active + position + n) % n`. Per slot: `scale 1 / 0.88 / 0.8`, `x = position*100%`, `y = 0 / 5% / 10%`, `rotate = position*2°`, `opacity 0` beyond ±1. Animate all with `duration 0.8, ease: [0.65, 0, 0.35, 1]`; z-index center-first. Non-center cards get a `bg-background/50 backdrop-blur-[1px]` overlay so the center pops. Autoplay 4s. ### Focus loop carousel (Embla) `useEmblaCarousel({ loop: true, align: "center" })`; inactive slides `opacity-70 scale-90`, active `opacity-100 scale-100`, `transition-all duration-500` — a center-stage loop for testimonials/media. (The standard row carousel — `dragFree: true`, progress bar, chevrons — is in composition.md.) ### Fanned card row (`HeroTiltedCards`) Static gallery that reads as 3D: 5 cards, alternating `±rotate-6` and `±translate-y-5`, overlapped with `-ml-15`, ascending z-index, `hover:scale-110 duration-500`. Mobile: swap to a marquee. ### Filter-swap animation (`FeaturesFilterGrid`) When a filter changes, don't re-sort in place — remount the grid with ``, key = active filter, and re-stagger the children (`staggerChildren` variants). The blink of motion reads as the grid "answering" the click. --- ## Navigation & page transitions ### Fullscreen curtain menu — `assets/NavbarFullscreen.tsx` The premium mobile/desktop menu: a full-viewport curtain drops from the top edge, oversized links rise in one by one. All the coordination details matter: - Curtain: `clip-path` polygon from zero-height top edge to full — `polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 0%, 0% 0%)` → `polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 100%, 0% 100%)`, `transition-[clip-path] duration-700 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.9,0,0.1,1)]`. Background `bg-foreground` (inverted), so the logo swaps `text-foreground ↔ text-background` in sync. - Links: `text-7xl md:text-9xl` inside `overflow-hidden`; `translateY(100%) → 0`, `transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.3, 1)`, open delay `0.3 + i*0.05`s, **close delay reversed** (`(n-1-i)*0.05`) so they exit bottom-up. Hairline `bg-background/20` dividers. - Link hover: label `group-hover:ml-4`, arrow `ArrowUpRight` `group-hover:rotate-45` — 300ms. - Hamburger→X: two `w-3 h-px` spans, `-translate-y-1`/`translate-y-1` ↔ `rotate-45`/`-rotate-45`. - Hygiene: `document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"` while open, Escape closes, nav itself is `fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none` with `pointer-events-auto` only on the bar + curtain. ### Page-transition swirl — `assets/PageTransitionSwirl.tsx` (GSAP DrawSVGPlugin) A brand-colored SVG spiral covers the viewport and "unwinds" itself away on page mount: - One long spiral `` in a fixed `inset-0 z-50 pointer-events-none` layer, `stroke="currentColor"` on a `text-primary-cta` wrapper, svg oversized `w-[130%] -top-[15%]` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`. - `gsap.set(path, { strokeWidth: "35%", drawSVG: "0% 100%" })` then `gsap.to(path, { drawSVG: "100% 100%", strokeWidth: "5%", duration: 1.25, ease: "power1.inOut", delay: 0.3 })` — the stroke thins as it erases, which is what makes it feel liquid. Register `gsap/DrawSVGPlugin`. - Mount it on route change (key it by pathname) for an instant "crafted" page swap. --- ## Loaders & clip-path reveals ### Clip-path wipe loader — in `assets/HeroVideoScroll.tsx` A full-screen loader that wipes the brand name in, then lifts away. - Text reveal: `clipPath: "inset(0% 100% 0% 0%)" → "inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)"`, `transition={{ duration: 2, ease: [0.76, 0, 0.24, 1] }}`. - Progress bar: `scaleX: 0 → 1`, `originX: 0`. - On complete: `AnimatePresence` exit `opacity: 0`, `duration 0.8, ease [0.76, 0, 0.24, 1]`. ### Clip-path expand reveal Loader panel that opens from an inset rounded rectangle to full-bleed: `clipPath: "inset(25% 20% 25% 20% round 24px)" → "inset(0% round 0px)"`, `duration 1.4, ease [0.76, 0, 0.24, 1]`. ### Brand panel loader (`LoaderReveal`) Solid `bg-background-accent` panel with logo + clip-path name wipe (3s), and a bottom progress bar with a signature detail: it **fills from the left** (`scaleX 0→1, originX: 0`, 3s) then **retracts to the right** (`originX: 1`, `scaleX→0`, 0.5s) before the whole panel exits `y: "-101%"`, `duration 1, ease [0.76, 0, 0.24, 1]`. Fill→retract→lift reads far better than a fade. **Signature easings worth reusing:** `[0.76, 0, 0.24, 1]` (dramatic in-out, for wipes/loaders), `[0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]` (soft overshoot-free ease-out, for content entrances), `[0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94]` (the slide-up default), `[0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]` (long luxurious settle — border glow, slow hero text), `[0.9, 0, 0.1, 1]` (hard curtain snap, for fullscreen menus), `[0.65, 0, 0.35, 1]` (symmetric in-out, for carousel slides), `[0.22, 0.68, 0, 1.2]` (playful overshoot, for 3D flips), `expo.out` / `back.out(2–3)` (GSAP, snappy fades / sticker pops). --- ## Zero-build vanilla HTML/CSS/JS & native CSS runtime — `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js` When building `MODE: EDITORIAL` (`MOTION 3`) showcase pages in Astro, Vanilla TypeScript, static HTML, or single-file HTML prototypes without React/Framer Motion/GSAP, pair `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js` (`initSilkKinetic()`) with these zero-dependency CSS primitives: ### 1. Entrance reveals & word-stagger headings (`[data-silk-reveal]`, `[data-silk-words]`) `initSilkKinetic()` splits `[data-silk-words]` into `` and sets `data-silk-visible="true"` once the element crosses `-20%` viewport margin (`IntersectionObserver` with automatic instant reveal when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active): ```css [data-silk-reveal], [data-silk-words] .silk-word { opacity: 0; transform: translate3d(0, 20px, 0); transition: opacity 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94); } [data-silk-words] .silk-word { display: inline-block; transition-delay: calc(var(--word-index, 0) * 40ms); } [data-silk-reveal][data-silk-visible="true"], [data-silk-words][data-silk-visible="true"] .silk-word { opacity: 1; transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { [data-silk-reveal], [data-silk-words] .silk-word { opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important; transition: none !important; } } ``` ### 2. Native CSS Scroll-Driven Parallax & Editorial Word-Fill (`animation-timeline: view()`) Zero-JavaScript scroll scrubbing in modern browsers using CSS Scroll-Driven Animations, wrapped in `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`: ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @supports (animation-timeline: view()) { .silk-parallax-front { animation: silk-drift-up linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% exit 100%; } .silk-reading-fill { color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 18%, transparent); animation: silk-word-brighten linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 20% cover 65%; } } } @keyframes silk-drift-up { from { transform: translate3d(0, 72px, 0); } to { transform: translate3d(0, -72px, 0); } } @keyframes silk-word-brighten { to { color: var(--foreground); } } ``` ### 3. Magnetic button & pointer-tracked conic border glow (`[data-silk-magnetic]`, `[data-silk-border-glow]`) `initSilkKinetic()` attaches passive pointer listeners (automatically disabled below `768px` and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`) and updates `--start` (angle in degrees) and `--active` (`0` or `1`) on `[data-silk-border-glow]` cards: ```css [data-silk-magnetic] { transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); will-change: transform; } [data-silk-border-glow] { position: relative; --start: 0; --active: 0; --spread: 40; } [data-silk-border-glow]::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: inherit; padding: 1.5px; pointer-events: none; opacity: var(--active, 0); transition: opacity 0.3s ease; background: conic-gradient( from calc((var(--start, 0) - var(--spread, 40)) * 1deg), transparent 0deg, var(--primary-cta) calc(var(--spread, 40) * 1deg), transparent calc(var(--spread, 40) * 2deg) ); -webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0); -webkit-mask-composite: xor; mask-composite: exclude; } ``` ### 4. View Transitions API Curtain Swap (`runSilkViewTransition`) Use `runSilkViewTransition(() => { ... })` from `assets/vanilla-kinetic.js` with native `::view-transition-old(root)` / `::view-transition-new(root)` clip-path wipes (`cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1)`, included in `assets/animations.css`), falling back to an instant DOM update when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is enabled: ```css @keyframes silk-curtain-in { from { clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0); } to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); } } @keyframes silk-curtain-out { from { opacity: 1; } to { opacity: 0; } } ::view-transition-old(root) { animation: 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1) both silk-curtain-out; } ::view-transition-new(root) { animation: 0.65s cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1) both silk-curtain-in; } ```

# silk — template references

23 worked reference compositions built from **this exact toolbox**. Pull one up as a starting
point: a coherent palette + font + section rhythm + effect set that already hangs together.
Triggered by `/silk-design Reference7` or "build this like the cream-and-espresso one". A number
resolves directly; a described mood resolves against the vibe line of each row.

## The contract — reference, don't clone
A referenced site is a **mood-board + wireframe, not a source file.** Take its **skin** and
**skeleton**; never its **flesh.**

- **Skin — take it:** palette, font, radius, card/button style, hero background, hover +
  text-animation, the signature effects.
- **Skeleton — take it loosely:** the section *rhythm* (the flow listed per site) as a
  starting sequence, re-ordered and trimmed to fit the real content. Not a pixel-copy of any
  layout.
- **Flesh — off-limits:** copy, images, brand, business specifics, and 1:1 layout. The new
  site has its own subject — write and lay it out for that.

The built-in foundation (Lenis root, 9-token system, fluid type, the one reveal config)
always applies underneath — see `SKILL.md`. The referenced site only decides the *look* and
*rhythm* on top of it.

## How to read a row
`ReferenceN` — vibe. Then palette / type / skin, the section **Flow**, and
the **Signature** effects worth stealing. Type is **Inter** (body) + **Inter Tight**
(headings) unless a row says *"Inter Tight throughout"* (a tighter, more editorial feel).
Every row is self-contained. For the full 9-token palette and the exact card/button CSS behind a
row's skin, read `templates/Reference<N>/theme.css` — a palette, a font, and three CSS recipes.
All compositions assume React + Vite + Tailwind v4 + motion + GSAP + Lenis.

---

# Sweetspot — Controlled Performance, Memory, Footprint & Network Optimization Gate

Optimizing an already working, stable system requires stricter discipline than fixing a broken one. Unconstrained optimization prompts across execution speed, Random-Access Memory (`RAM`), disk footprint, or network Input/Output (`I/O`) often trigger three failure modes in language models: inventing unmeasured micro-optimizations that degrade readability, silently breaking edge-case behavior or data fidelity, or mutating a project's architecture and purpose without asking. `sweetspot` enforces **controlled, behavior-preserving optimization** across three universal local resource axes—**Time (Speed/Latency)**, **Memory (`RAM` Footprint)**, and **Disk (Binary, Bundle & Storage Footprint)**—plus a **Conditional 4th Axis for networked systems—Network (`I/O` Download/Upload Bandwidth & Round-Trip Time (`RTT`) Latency)**, backed by multi-file hot-path discovery, repeatable measurements, explicit **Cross-Axis Trade-off** governance, and an honest stop condition when a system reaches its **Pareto Frontier** (the holistic sweet spot where all active axes meet without structural compromise).

---

## 1. Core Invariants

1. **Working Baseline Prerequisite:** Apply `sweetspot` only to systems whose functional behavior is currently working and stable. If tests are failing or the system crashes, route to `skills/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md` first.
2. **Behavior & Data Preservation (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9):** A controlled optimization leaves every observable contract identical: return values, output formatting, error boundaries, determinism, side effects, wire protocol compatibility, and stored data fidelity. Never delete user data, audit logs, or required assets to claim a memory, disk, or network reduction.
3. **Measure Before and After (`GEMINI.md` Rule 8):** Intuition about where time, memory, disk space, or network bandwidth is spent holds zero evidentiary weight. Every optimization claim requires a repeatable before-and-after measurement on the target machine (using deterministic loopback harnesses or exact payload/request counters for network boundaries, never noisy external internet jitter).
4. **Holistic Multi-Axis Default, Explicit Axis Flags & Trade-Off Discipline:**
   * **Holistic Intersection Mode (`--all` / `--holistic`, or No Flag — Default):** When the user requests general optimization without restricting to a single axis (such as *"optimize this game"*, *"bu oyunu/yazılımı optimize et"*, `/sweetspot`, or `/sweetspot --all`), target the **Holistic Multi-Axis Intersection** simultaneously:
     * **3-Axis Local Intersection (`Time + Memory + Disk`):** Applied automatically when Step 1 detects a purely local/offline codebase with no network boundaries.
     * **4-Axis Networked Intersection (`Time + Memory + Disk + Network`):** Activated automatically inside Holistic Mode whenever Step 1 detects network boundaries (Hypertext Transfer Protocol (`HTTP`), WebSocket, Remote Procedure Call (`gRPC`), socket clients/servers, remote database/service queries, multiplayer netcode, or web bundle/asset delivery).
     * First eliminate **joint slack**—dead work, per-frame allocation churn, duplicate in-memory buffers, unstreamed full-file reads, redundant `N+1` network round trips, uncompressed wire payloads, and unused dependencies or assets—that improves all active axes together (or improves at least one axis by `>= 1%` with `0%` regression beyond `< 1%` noise on all other active axes) until the software reaches its **Pareto Frontier**.
   * **Single-Axis Mode (`--time`, `--memory`, `--disk`, `--net` or Natural Language) & Cross-Axis Trade-Off Gate:** When the user passes an explicit single-axis flag or names a specific primary axis in natural language, focus on that primary axis and treat all remaining active axes as non-regressing guardrails (`< 1%` noise floor). Once the Pareto Frontier is reached in either mode, any further gain that requires trading away another resource axis beyond `< 1%` noise (such as caching in memory or disk to cut network round trips, spending extra processor time on high-ratio compression to shrink upload/download bandwidth, or adding cold-start decompression latency to shrink disk size) is classified as **Zone 2** and requires explicit user approval before editing code.

| Flag | Alias | Mode & Primary Target Axis | Non-Regressing Guardrail Axes (`< 1%` Noise) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *(none)* or `--all` | `--holistic` | **Holistic Intersection (Default):** `Time + Memory + Disk` (plus **Conditional Axis 4: `Network`** whenever the target structure has network boundaries) | All active axes must remain `<= 0%` regression (`< 1%` noise) while at least one improves `>= 1%` |
| `--time` | `--speed` | **Axis 1 — Execution Speed & Latency** (wall time, frame rate, cold start) | `Memory`, `Disk`, and (if networked) `Network` |
| `--memory` | `--ram` | **Axis 2 — Memory Footprint** (peak Resident Set Size (`RSS`), retained heap, allocation churn) | `Time`, `Disk`, and (if networked) `Network` |
| `--disk` | `--size` | **Axis 3 — Disk, Bundle & Storage Footprint** (binary, bundle, database size) | `Time`, `Memory`, and (if networked) `Network` |
| `--net` | `--network` | **Axis 4 — Network I/O** (download/upload payload bytes, request count, `RTT` latency) | `Time`, `Memory`, and `Disk` |
5. **Domain Co-Loading & White-Box vs. Black-Box Tool Routing:**
   * **Real-Time Game & Simulation Co-Loading:** When the target is a game, interactive canvas application, or real-time simulation loop, co-load `skills/game-engineering/SKILL.md` before Step 1 profiling so fixed-timestep determinism, zero per-frame allocation, and headless tick verification govern every measurement and edit.
   * **Source Code (`code_map.py`) vs. Shipped Artifact (`reverse-engineer-anything`) Boundary:** When source code is available (white-box analysis), map multi-file call graphs and dataflow using `scripts/code_map.py` and native language profilers; never invoke the `reverse-engineer-anything` plugin for ordinary source-repository analysis. Route to `reverse-engineer-anything` (`inspect_artifact`, `inspect_binary_layout`, `analyze_javascript_application`, or `analyze_web_bundle`) **only** when inspecting a shipped binary, compiled executable without source, mobile package, Electron archive, or stripped bundle where standard source tools and `stat`/`size` cannot explain internal section or payload bloat.
6. **Honest Sweet-Spot Declaration:** Finding that no meaningful optimization is possible within the current scope—or that further gain requires changing the system's identity or trading away another resource—is a first-class, successful engineering outcome, never a failure to hide.

---

## 2. Step 1: Map Multi-File Architecture, Pin Behavior & Measure the Active-Axis Baseline

Before proposing or writing any optimization edit:

1. **Map the Multi-File Hot-Path, Network Boundaries & Dependency Graph (`scripts/code_map.py`):**
   * Never optimize the first inspected file in isolation when a software project or game spans multiple connected files and modules (such as entrypoint, game loop, physics, entity management, rendering, network transport, data loaders, and asset pipelines).
   * Starting from the application entrypoint or main update loop, map the connected call graph, dataflow, and blast radius across all participating files using `python3 scripts/code_map.py profile <symbol>`, `callers <symbol>`, `flow <symbol>`, and `blast-radius <symbol>` (or `python3 ~/.local/share/antigravity-harness/runtime/scripts/code_map.py`). Identify cross-file bottlenecks—such as producer modules allocating transient objects consumed by downstream loop modules, redundant serialization across module boundaries, or sequential network call chains—before choosing optimization targets.
2. **Pin Observable Behavior (`skills/refactoring/SKILL.md` §3):**
   * Run the existing test suite covering the target path across all coupled modules.
   * If the hot path lacks seam tests, write characterization tests that lock exact current outputs across representative and boundary inputs before touching production code.
3. **Establish a Repeatable Multi-Axis Benchmark Sensor (Holistic 3/4-Axis Default or Primary + Guardrail Axes):**
   * Construct a deterministic measurement command capturing all active axes in **Holistic Mode** (`Time + Memory + Disk`, plus **Axis 4: `Network`** whenever network boundaries exist) or the primary axis plus guardrail checks in **Single-Axis Mode**:
     * **Axis 1 — Execution Speed & Latency (Time):**
       * *Scripts, Functions & Backends:* Wall-clock execution time (`p50` median and `p95` tail latency across `N >= 5` runs after warm-up) using `hyperfine`, `time`, or `go test -bench`, plus query execution plans (`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`).
       * *Real-Time Games & Interactive Loops:* Frame-step execution time in milliseconds (`stepTick` / `update` + `render` budget against `16.67 ms` for 60 frames per second (`FPS`) or `8.33 ms` for 120 frames per second).
       * *Command-Line Interface (`CLI`) Tools & Executables:* Cold-start versus warm-start launch latency (`time`, `hyperfine`, `python3 -X importtime`) and dynamic library load count.
     * **Axis 2 — Memory Footprint (`RAM`):**
       * *Peak & Retained Memory:* Peak Resident Set Size (`RSS` via `/usr/bin/time -v` or `ps`) and peak heap allocation (`tracemalloc`, `go test -benchmem`, `valgrind --tool=massif`, or runtime heap snapshots).
       * *Hot-Loop & Per-Request Allocation Churn:* Allocation count and bytes allocated per frame, tick, or request (`skills/game-engineering/SKILL.md`), verifying that retained heap plateaus across repeated iterations rather than growing unboundedly.
     * **Axis 3 — Disk, Bundle & Storage Footprint (Space):**
       * *Compiled Executables & Libraries:* On-disk binary size (`stat`, `size`, `bloaty`) and section breakdown (`.text`, `.rodata`, `.data`, debug symbols) across the target Operating System (`OS`); if inspecting a stripped or packaged binary artifact whose internal bloat cannot be resolved from source or `size`, use `reverse-engineer-anything` (`inspect_binary_layout` or `inspect_artifact`).
       * *Application Bundles, Packages & Containers:* Bundled asset and script/stylesheet payload sizes (uncompressed and compressed via `gzip` or `brotli`), dependency tree weight, and container image layer sizes (or `analyze_web_bundle` / `analyze_javascript_application` when analyzing packaged web or Electron artifacts).
       * *Runtime Persistent Storage:* On-disk database, cache, and state file footprint (`du -b`, SQLite page count and freelist ratio) under a deterministic workload.
     * **Axis 4 — Network I/O: Download/Upload Bandwidth & Round-Trip Latency (Conditional in `--all` Holistic Mode; Primary in `--net` Mode):**
       * *Download & Upload Payload Volume (Ingress / Egress Bytes):* Total uncompressed and wire-compressed (`gzip`, `brotli`, `zstd`) download and upload bytes transferred per user journey, request cycle, or state sync, plus payload schema bloat (over-fetching unused fields or duplicate metadata).
       * *Round-Trip Time (`RTT`) & Request Waterfall Depth:* Sequential round-trip depth, connection and Transport Layer Security (`TLS`) handshake count, `N+1` request waterfalls, and local loopback `p50` median and `p95` tail latency (or `inspect_web_network_capture` / `inspect_packet_capture` when inspecting captured browser or packet traces).
       * *Real-Time Netcode & Streaming Throughput:* Packet or message frequency (tick/snapshot rate), header-to-payload ratio, and stream backpressure under a deterministic workload.
       * *Deterministic Loopback & Counter Rule (`GEMINI.md` Rule 8):* Never benchmark against live external internet jitter; measure against a deterministic local loopback server, recorded replay fixture, or exact wire-byte, request-count, and waterfall-depth counters so the `< 1%` noise floor holds.
   * Record the exact baseline numbers across all active axes (`Time`, `Memory`, `Disk`, and `Network` when applicable), and locate the actual hot spots or bloat sources across the connected module graph using a profiler, runtime call-edge tracer (`python3 scripts/code_map.py trace <script.py>` or `python3 ~/.local/share/antigravity-harness/runtime/scripts/code_map.py trace <script.py>`), heap/section analyzer, network trace inspector, query plan (`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`), or startup import timer (`python3 -X importtime`).

---

## 3. Step 2: The 3-Zone Sweet-Spot Classification Gate

Once the baseline profile is captured, classify every identified optimization opportunity into one of three explicit zones **before editing production code**:

| Zone | Classification | Defining Criteria | Required Agent Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Zone 1** | **Controlled Optimization (In-Scope / Pareto Sweet Spot)** | Preserves exact observable behavior, public interfaces, wire contracts, data fidelity, portability, and the system's core architecture while eliminating joint slack across all active axes or targeting a measured bottleneck above the noise floor (`>= 1%` improvement on at least one active axis—Time, Memory, Disk, or Network—with `0%` regression beyond `< 1%` noise on all remaining active axes). | Present the bottleneck proof and expected gain (or execute directly if the user already authorized in-scope optimization) and verify via Step 4 (Section 5) until the **Pareto Frontier** is reached. |
| **Zone 2** | **Trade-Off or Identity-Shifting Optimization** | Further Time, Memory, Disk, or Network improvement beyond the Pareto Frontier is achievable, **but** requires either: (a) a **cross-axis resource trade-off** beyond `< 1%` noise (e.g., increasing peak memory or disk usage via caching to cut network downloads/round trips, spending extra processor time on heavy compression to shrink upload/download bandwidth, batching uploads at the cost of higher per-message latency, or adding cold-start decompression latency to shrink disk size); or (b) altering the software's purpose, problem domain, feature contract, numerical precision, lossy asset compression, cache eviction semantics, public file/wire format, or deployment layout. | **STOP.** Do not modify code. Explain the exact trade-off (`Target Axis | Proposed Shift | Cross-Axis or Feature Cost | Expected Gain`) and ask for explicit user approval via `ask_question` or direct confirmation. |
| **Zone 3** | **Already at the Sweet Spot (Pareto Frontier) / Out of Scope** | (a) All joint Zone 1 opportunities are exhausted and the software stands on its **Multi-Axis Pareto Frontier**, bounded by hardware, `OS` syscall floors, minimum runtime footprint, network protocol headers, or information-theoretic entropy (Amdahl's Law or compression ceiling); (b) the only remaining hotspots or bloat sources lie outside the user's permitted scope; or (c) remaining micro-optimizations yield `< 1%` gain while reducing code clarity. | **STOP (`GEMINI.md` Rule 8 Null-Action Invariant).** Modify zero further files. Deliver an honest **Sweet-Spot Report** with the multi-axis profiling numbers proving why the structure is at its optimal Pareto sweet spot. |

---

## 4. Step 3: Domain Playbooks for Zone 1 Controlled Optimizations

When Zone 1 opportunities exist, prefer structural, readable wins in this order:

### A. Execution Speed: Scripts, Data Pipelines & Backend Services
* **Algorithmic & Lookup Complexity:** Replace repeated linear scans ($O(N \times M)$) inside loops with pre-indexed sets or hash maps ($O(N + M)$) when the index allocation stays within `< 1%` of peak memory (otherwise request Zone 2 trade-off approval).
* **Loop-Invariant Hoisting & Compilation:** Hoist regular expression compilation, configuration parsing, filesystem checks, and constant object construction out of inner loops.
* **Batching & Streaming:** Replace `N+1` sequential queries or network/disk calls with batched reads/writes; use iterators or streaming buffers instead of materializing multi-megabyte intermediate lists in memory when only aggregates are needed.
* **Cold-Start Import Hygiene (Python / Node.js):** Defer heavy, non-essential module imports (`pandas`, plotting libraries, cloud software development kits, optional subcommands) inside the specific functions that use them so `CLI` startup and `--help` remain instantaneous.

### B. Execution Speed & Allocation Churn: Real-Time Games & Interactive Simulations (`skills/game-engineering/SKILL.md`)
* **Zero Per-Frame Heap Allocation:** Eliminate `.map()`, `.filter()`, object spreads, and temporary vector instantiations inside 60–120 Hz `update` and `render` loops; reuse pre-allocated scratch buffers across coupled loop modules.
* **Object Pooling & Broad-Phase Culling:** Pool transient entities (particles, projectiles, damage text) across entity producer and consumer modules, and apply spatial grid / bounding-box culling before narrow-phase collision math.
* **Render State Batching:** Group draw calls by texture/material/fillStyle and bridge state to Document Object Model (`DOM`) overlays only on discrete events rather than every animation frame.

### C. Execution Speed: Compiled Executables, Packaging & Cross-`OS` Responsiveness
* **Startup Critical-Path Trimming:** Defer non-critical disk scans, telemetry hooks, font/asset preloading, and background worker spawning until after the initial window render or first command response.
* **Semantics-Preserving Compiler & Linker Flags:** Enable release optimization levels (`-O2` / `-O3`, Rust `codegen-units = 1` with Link-Time Optimization (`LTO`) `lto = "thin"`, Go `-ldflags="-s -w"`, dead-section elimination `--gc-sections`) while strictly forbidding unsafe floating-point flags (`-ffast-math`) unless explicitly approved under Zone 2.
* **Packaging & Extraction Overhead:** Identify when slow executable launch on Linux, macOS, or Windows is caused by self-extracting archive decompression to a temporary directory on every cold start (such as single-file bundled runtimes). Report the measured extraction cost vs. actual application startup time, and seek Zone 2 approval before changing the distribution format.

### D. Memory Footprint (`RAM`) & Allocation Hygiene
* **Data Layout & Object Overhead Compaction:** Replace heavyweight dynamic dictionaries or boxed object wrappers on high-cardinality records with `__slots__`, `namedtuple`, compact `dataclass(slots=True)`, typed arrays (`array`, `Float64Array`), or flat parallel buffers.
* **Streaming & Generator Pipelines:** Replace full-file reads (`.read()`, `.readlines()`) and multi-pass list comprehensions with single-pass generators, chunked stream readers, or database cursors so peak memory stays $O(1)$ or $O(\text{chunk})$ instead of $O(N)$.
* **Reference Release & Duplicate Buffer Elimination:** Clear dead references to large intermediate buffers as soon as their scope ends, and avoid retaining duplicate raw, parsed, and serialized copies of the same payload in memory simultaneously. (Changing an unbounded cache to evict entries that callers rely on for state requires Zone 2 approval; bounding a pure memoization cache must preserve exact outputs.)
* **Lazy Asset & Module Materialization:** Load heavy lookup tables, localization bundles, or optional submodules only when the code path that requires them is actually invoked.

### E. Disk, Bundle & Persistent Storage Footprint
* **Binary Symbol & Dead-Section Pruning:** Strip non-essential symbol tables and debug sections in release builds (`strip`, Go `-ldflags="-s -w"`, Rust `strip = "symbols"`), enable `--gc-sections` with `-fdata-sections -ffunction-sections`, and avoid statically linking unused subsystems.
* **Bundle Tree-Shaking & Dependency Diet:** Replace monolithic barrel imports with direct submodule imports so bundlers can tree-shake dead code, and remove unused static assets, duplicate font weights, or orphaned lockfile dependencies verified to have zero callers via `python3 scripts/code_map.py callers <symbol>`.
* **Lossless Storage & Database Compaction:** Reclaim fragmented freelist pages (`VACUUM` on SQLite when safe offline), deduplicate identical stored blobs via content-addressed references where the schema already supports it, and apply deterministic lossless compression to internal caches without altering public file formats. (Switching public file formats, applying lossy media compression, or truncating logs/history requires Zone 2 approval.)

### F. Network I/O: Download/Upload Bandwidth & Round-Trip Latency
* **Request Waterfall Flattening & Coalescing:** Collapse sequential `N+1` network round trips into batched queries, parallel independent fetches (`Promise.all`, `asyncio.gather`, `errgroup`), or single-trip bulk reads/writes, and deduplicate identical in-flight requests triggered simultaneously across components.
* **Connection Reuse & Multiplexing:** Reuse persistent client sessions (`HTTP Keep-Alive` connection pools, multiplexed `HTTP/2` or `HTTP/3` streams, persistent `gRPC` channels, or pooled database sockets) instead of paying fresh connection and handshake latency on every request.
* **Download & Upload Payload Diet (Zero-Semantic-Loss):** Enable standard lossless transport compression (`brotli`, `gzip`, `zstd`) when processor and memory overhead stays within `< 1%` guardrails, omit unused fields in internal queries (over-fetching elimination), and stream chunked uploads/downloads instead of buffering multi-megabyte request/response bodies in memory. (Mutating public wire schemas, introducing lossy payload quantization, or delaying real-time uploads via aggressive batching windows requires Zone 2 approval.)
* **Conditional Fetching & Delta Sync:** Leverage protocol-level cache revalidation (`ETag` / `If-None-Match` returning `304 Not Modified`) and send incremental state deltas rather than full-state snapshots across real-time WebSocket or multiplayer loops when wire compatibility is preserved.

---

## 5. Step 4: Single-Hypothesis Atomic Slices & Append-Only Experiment Ledger

Execute approved optimizations under strict experimental control (`skills/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md` alignment):

1. **Single-Hypothesis Isolation (Including Coupled Cross-File Atomic Slices):** Apply one optimization hypothesis at a time. When a single bottleneck spans multiple coupled files (for example, introducing an object pool across loop modules or coalescing sequential client fetches with a shared connection pool), update the **minimal coupled cross-file atomic slice** required by that single hypothesis in one measured attempt, and record all touched `file:line` coordinates in the ledger. Never bundle unrelated performance, memory, size, or network hypotheses into a single unmeasured diff.
2. **Re-Run Pinning Tests & Multi-Axis Benchmark:** Immediately run the characterization/unit test suite (must exit `0` with zero modified assertions per `GEMINI.md` Rule 9) and re-run the exact Step 1 benchmark command under identical load conditions to verify both primary gain and guardrail axes.
3. **Append-Only Experiment Ledger & Simplicity Criterion:** Record every attempt in the canonical 7-column ledger shared with `skills/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
| Attempt | Zone | Hypothesis & Target (`file:line`) | Diff Summary | Baseline | Measured | Status: KEEP/REVERT |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `#1` | Zone 1 | Pool projectiles across loop (`entities.js:42`, `physics.js:118`) | Reuse pre-allocated pool instead of per-tick instantiation | `14.2 ms/tick, 96 MB` | `8.9 ms/tick (-37.3%), 54 MB (-43.8%)` | `KEEP` |
| `#2` | Zone 1 | Stream CSV rows (`loader.py:84`) | Replace `readlines()` list with generator | `312 MB RSS` | `28 MB RSS (-91.0%)` | `KEEP` |
| `#3` | Zone 1 | Strip release symbols (`Makefile:19`) | Add `-ldflags="-s -w"` to build target | `18.4 MB bin` | `12.1 MB bin (-34.2%)` | `KEEP` |
| `#4` | Zone 1 | Coalesce `N+1` user-item fetches & reuse session (`sync.py:61`, `api.py:29`) | Batch item IDs into single request over pooled `HTTP` session | `14 RTTs, 480 KB dl, 62 ms` | `2 RTTs (-85.7%), 112 KB dl (-76.7%), 11 ms (-82.3%)` | `KEEP` |
| `#5` | Zone 1 | Unroll 4-element matrix loop (`sim.py:188`) | Inline 4 multiply-add expressions | `3.8 ms/tick` | `3.78 ms/tick (-0.5%)` | `REVERT (Noise < 1%)` |
```

* **The Simplicity Criterion & Termination Cap (`GEMINI.md` Rule 13):**
  * Any change that adds code complexity for noise-level gain (`< 1%` across active Time, Memory, Disk, and Network axes, or that regresses any non-target guardrail axis beyond `< 1%` noise without Zone 2 approval) is immediately reverted (`REVERT`).
  * Any change that simplifies code or deletes dead work/bloat while achieving equal or better measured metrics (`>= 0%`) is kept (`KEEP`).
  * Never stack a subsequent attempt on top of a reverted or unmeasured edit.
  * **3-Strike Sweet-Spot Circuit Breaker:** After 3 consecutive `REVERT` attempts (or when all profiled Zone 1 hotspots/bloat sources `>= 1%` are exhausted and the software reaches its Pareto Frontier), halt code edits immediately and transition to **Zone 3** (`Sweet-Spot Report`).

---

## 6. Triggers and Invocations

* **Slash Commands & Axis Flags:**
  * `/sweetspot`, `/optimize`, `/sweetspot --all`, `/sweetspot --holistic` *(Holistic Default: 3-axis `Time + Memory + Disk` on local software; automatically expands to 4-axis `Time + Memory + Disk + Network` when network boundaries exist)*
  * `/sweetspot --time` (alias `--speed`), `/sweetspot --memory` (alias `--ram`), `/sweetspot --disk` (alias `--size`), `/sweetspot --net` (alias `--network`)
* **Natural Language Triggers:** *"sweetspot analizi yap"*, *"bu oyunu optimize et"*, *"bu yazılımı/projeyi optimize et"*, *"bunu yapıyı bozmadan hızlandır"*, *"performans optimizasyonu yap"*, *"kare hızını artır"*, *"daha hızlı açılsın"*, *"bellek kullanımını düşür"*, *"RAM optimizasyonu yap"*, *"disk alanını küçült"*, *"dosya/paket boyutunu küçült"*, *"ağ optimizasyonu yap"*, *"indirme ve yükleme boyutunu küçült"*, *"indirme/yükleme hızını optimize et"*, *"ağ gecikmesini (latency) düşür"*, *"bant genişliği optimizasyonu"*, *"optimize this game/app/project"*, *"optimize this for speed, memory, disk size, or network bandwidth/latency without breaking behavior"*.

# Technical Writing: Verified, Mode-Separated Documentation

Technical documentation fails when it mixes learning tutorials with exhaustive reference tables, presents unverified commands that fail on copy-paste, or buries prerequisites beneath marketing filler. This skill enforces structural mode separation, executable example verification, and high-signal technical prose.

## 1. Classify the Document Mode Before Writing (Diataxis)

Every document or top-level section serves exactly one of four reader states. State the chosen mode before drafting and never mix two modes inside the same section:

1. **Tutorial (Learning-Oriented):**
   - *Reader state:* A newcomer learning by doing under guidance.
   - *Contract:* Walk through one deterministic, end-to-end concrete example from a stated starting state to a visible result. Omit edge-case branches, configuration alternatives, and conceptual digressions; link out to Reference or Explanation sections instead.
2. **How-To Guide (Task-Oriented):**
   - *Reader state:* A practitioner with a specific goal or operational problem (including incident runbooks).
   - *Contract:* Start with prerequisites and target outcome; provide numbered, copy-pasteable steps and the verification command that proves the task succeeded; include rollback or recovery steps for mutating operations.
3. **Reference (Information-Oriented):**
   - *Reader state:* A developer looking up exact signatures, flags, parameters, return types, defaults, or error codes while working.
   - *Contract:* Mirror the structure of the codebase or Command-Line Interface (CLI) parser. Every public flag, parameter, configuration key, default value, type, and error status must match the source of truth verbatim.
4. **Explanation (Understanding-Oriented):**
   - *Reader state:* An engineer evaluating architecture, trade-offs, design rationale, or system boundaries.
   - *Contract:* Explain causal mechanisms, constraints, and why a design was chosen over alternatives; keep step-by-step commands out of conceptual explanations.

## 2. Executable Documentation Gate (Zero Unverified Snippets)

Code blocks and shell commands in documentation are executable contracts, not decorative illustrations:

- **Source-of-Truth Verification:** Before documenting a function signature, CLI flag, environment variable, or configuration key, inspect the actual parser, schema, or type definition in the repository (`skills/harness/SKILL.md` §2). Never write flags, options, or subcommands from memory.
- **Execute or Parse Every Snippet:** Run shell commands (`--help`, `--dry-run`, or in a temporary directory) and parse syntax-checked code snippets or configuration blocks (`.json`, `.toml`, `.yaml`) before delivery. If a snippet requires external credentials or production services and cannot be executed locally, declare it explicitly in the Verification Gap Declaration (`GEMINI.md` Rule 8).
- **Show Input and Expected Output:** Separate the command the user runs from the output it prints (either in separate blocks or with explicit comments) so copying the block never feeds output lines back into the shell.
- **Local Link Integrity:** Every relative link and `file://` reference must resolve to an existing file in the workspace (enforced by automated gates), and any `#heading` fragment must match an actual heading slug in the target document (verified during review).

## 3. Cognitive Load & Prose Hygiene

- **Lead with the Prerequisite and Outcome:** Open every guide with what must already be installed or configured and what state the reader will reach at the end.
- **One Concept Per Step:** Each numbered step performs one logical action and states how to verify it before moving on.
- **Abbreviation Discipline (`GEMINI.md` Rule 4):** Spell out every domain term or protocol in full before its abbreviation on first use, and keep at most one abbreviation per sentence.
- **Anti-Slop Technical Profile:** Run `skills/antislop-copywriting/scripts/check_synthetic_markers.py --profile technical` (or `~/.gemini/config/skills/antislop-copywriting/scripts/check_synthetic_markers.py --profile technical`, with `--lang tr` or `--lang auto` for Turkish documentation) on drafted Markdown files to strip signposting announcements (*"In this section we will explore"*, *"İşte bilmeniz gerekenler"*), chatbot leftovers, and brochure inflation while preserving normal engineering tables and lists (`skills/antislop-copywriting/SKILL.md`).

## 4. Changelog & Release Note Discipline (`CHANGELOG.md`)

When authoring release notes or `CHANGELOG.md` entries:

- **Order by Reader Impact:** Group entries under `Breaking Changes`, `Security`, `Added`, `Changed`, `Fixed`, and `Deprecated`.
- **Actionable Breaking Changes:** Every breaking change must show the old usage, the new usage, and the exact migration command or edit required.
- **Observable Behavior Only:** Describe what changed for callers, operators, or end users. Do not list internal variable renames or test-file restructuring as user-facing features.

## 5. Delivery Checklist

Before delivering technical documentation, verify:
- [ ] Each section follows a single Diataxis mode (Tutorial, How-To, Reference, or Explanation) without mode mixing.
- [ ] Every documented CLI flag, configuration key, and function signature was verified against the codebase source of truth.
- [ ] Code snippets and structured configuration blocks were executed or syntax-parsed, or declared under `Not verified` (`GEMINI.md` Rule 8).
- [ ] Relative links and repository paths resolve cleanly (`scripts/meta_audit.py` Pass 2).
- [ ] `python3 skills/antislop-copywriting/scripts/check_synthetic_markers.py --profile technical <file>` (or `python3 ~/.gemini/config/skills/antislop-copywriting/scripts/check_synthetic_markers.py --profile technical <file>`) exits `0`.

# Test Design

A test exists to catch a specific break. This skill is the reference for writing one that does: what a good test is, where it goes, how the expected value is obtained, when a mock is allowed, and the rules of the red → green loop. Worked examples are in [examples.md](./examples.md).

## 1. Scope and the Immutable Test Invariant

These rules govern the tests you write now. Existing tests are frozen (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9, enforced by `agy-guard test-boundary verify` / `python3 scripts/verify_invariants.py --test-boundary`): a weak existing test is reported to the user, never edited, relaxed, or deleted without explicit user authorization; a new assertion goes into a new test (in `--mode bugfix`, existing test files must remain 100% byte-identical and new regression tests go into a new test file; in `--mode tdd`, existing test files may be extended with pure line additions that never mutate or remove existing lines).

## 2. The Loop: Red, Then Green

1. **Find the project's own test command** before running anything (`GEMINI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`).
2. **Write one failing test** at a public seam for one behavior.
3. **Run it and confirm the red.** All three must hold:
   - the test *fails*; it does not error on an import, a syntax typo, or a missing fixture;
   - the failure message is the expected assertion failure;
   - it fails because the behavior is missing or wrong, which is what the test is about.

   A test that passes immediately tests behavior that already exists: it does not protect this change. State that explicitly and rework it.
4. **Write the minimum production code** that makes it pass (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9 & Rule 18: general logic only, never hardcoded test return literals or test-runner detection). No speculative features and no code for tests you have not written yet.
5. **Run the whole suite** and inspect the output.
6. Repeat, one vertical slice at a time. Do not write all tests first and all implementation afterwards: bulk pre-written tests describe imagined behavior and lock in internal structure before the implementation has taught you anything.

A regression test for a bug fix reproduces the reported symptom and fails on the unfixed code (`skills/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md` Phase 1 & Phase 5). Restructuring belongs after green, as a separate step (`skills/refactoring/SKILL.md`).

## 3. Seams: Where Tests Go

A seam is the public boundary where behavior is observed without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against volatile private internals (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9): internal helpers may change completely while the seam test remains untouched. A test that breaks during a behavior-preserving refactor was coupled to private implementation details.

Put testing effort on critical paths, state transitions, and complex branching logic. For Tier 2 and Tier 3 changes, list the target seams under test in the implementation plan (`skills/harness/SKILL.md` §4.A & §4.E).

## 4. Name the Break Before Writing the Body

Answer first: **which production defect should make this test fail, and is that change a bug or an intentional design decision?** A test earns its place by catching a wrong branch, a missing side effect, a swapped argument, a boundary violation, or a broken contract.

| Your answer | What to do |
|---|---|
| "I cannot name one" | Redesign the test around an observable behavior at the public seam |
| "The source text changed" | Execute the code and assert its return value, side effects, or exit code; never assert by grepping production source text |
| "Only an intentional decision" (a constant's value, exact prose wording, private structure) | That is a brittle change detector: it fires on deliberate redesign and sleeps through real bugs. Test the behavior that depends on the decision |

Test the contract your own code establishes at its boundaries (the route registered, the query emitted, the payload produced), not the framework's own documented mechanics. Constructors, getters, constants, and plain pass-through functions earn a test only when they validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce an invariant, or cause a side effect.

## 5. Expected Values Come From Outside the Code Under Test

Use concrete literals and hand-verified fixtures; a table of cases with literal inputs and literal expected outputs is the preferred shape. Never compute the expected value inside the test by calling the function under test, calling its internal helpers, or copying its formula into the assertion—doing so creates a tautology that passes even when the formula is wrong.

## 6. Mocks at System Boundaries Only

Mock at **system boundaries only**: external network services, wall-clock time, randomness, and where necessary out-of-process databases or filesystems. Never mock your own domain modules, internal collaborators, or the function under test.

- **Understand the real method's side effects first**; replace only the slow or external transport layer below the state transitions the test depends on.
- **The mock earns zero assertions.** Asserting that a mock was called or returned its configured literal proves nothing about the system's observable outcome. Assert the real component's output or state transition.
- **Mirror real payload shapes completely:** a partial mock fixture passes unit tests while downstream code that reads an omitted field crashes in production.
- **Give each boundary branch its own fixture:** separate explicit fixtures for success, error, timeout, and malformed response cases.
- **Deterministic wall-clock & time-to-live anchors:** never compare live `datetime.now()`, `time.time()`, or `Date.now()` against hardcoded calendar dates or fixed International Organization for Standardization (ISO) timestamps. Inject an explicit `now` clock anchor into the function under test or compute fixture timestamps relative to a deterministic anchor via `timedelta`.
- **No test-only methods in production code:** cleanup or reset helpers needed only by tests belong in `tests/` utilities, never on production classes.
- When mock setup exceeds half the test body, switch to a real in-memory or local integration fixture.

## 7. The Mental Mutation Pass

Before finishing, mentally apply five realistic mutations to the production code you wrote; at least one test must fail for each:

- a wrong constant or swapped argument;
- an inverted conditional branch (`<` vs `<=`, `if` vs `unless`);
- a skipped state transition or side effect;
- an empty, `null`, or default return;
- missing boundary validation for zero, empty, negative, unauthorized, or malformed input.

If a mutation would leave the test suite green, the behavior is unprotected or the new assertion is tautological.

## 8. Warning Signs (Anti-Patterns)

- Setup and assertion reference the exact same mutated object reference, guaranteeing equality.
- The test can fail only via an unhandled crash or syntax error (`assert result is not None` without checking value).
- The test fails on every intentional refactor and never on accidental logic regressions.
- Expected values are computed by loops, builders, or the production helper itself.
- The test reads production source files as strings or asserts only that a symbol name is absent.
- The test would still pass if the business logic were deleted and only the mock/framework remained.
- The test compares live wall-clock time (`datetime.now()`, `time.time()`, `Date.now()`) against a hardcoded calendar date or fixed ISO timestamp ("time-bomb" test that flips outcome as real calendar dates advance).
- A production method or environment branch exists solely to detect or serve the test suite (`GEMINI.md` Rule 9).

# Test design: examples

Python is used for illustration; the rules are the same in every language.

## Behaviour through the interface

```python
# Coupled to the implementation: breaks on a refactor, says nothing about the result
def test_checkout_calls_payment_process(monkeypatch):
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(payment_service, "process", lambda total: calls.append(total))
    checkout(cart, method)
    assert calls == [cart.total]

# Observable behaviour at the seam
def test_user_can_check_out_with_a_valid_cart():
    cart = Cart()
    cart.add(product)
    assert checkout(cart, method).status == "confirmed"
```

## Verify through the interface, not around it

```python
# Bypasses the interface: passes while get_user is broken
def test_create_user_saves_a_row():
    create_user(name="Alice")
    assert db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", ["Alice"]) is not None

# Through the interface
def test_created_user_can_be_retrieved():
    user = create_user(name="Alice")
    assert get_user(user.id).name == "Alice"
```

## Independent expected values

```python
# Tautology: the expected value is computed the way the code computes it
def test_total_sums_line_items():
    items = [{"price": 10}, {"price": 5}]
    assert calculate_total(items) == sum(item["price"] for item in items)

# Mirror assertion: the same builder produces both sides
def test_search_query():
    assert build_search_query(tag="urgent") == build_search_query(tag="urgent")

# A known literal
def test_total_sums_line_items():
    assert calculate_total([{"price": 10}, {"price": 5}]) == 15

# A table of literal cases
CASES = [("", 0), ("a", 1), ("a b", 2), ("  a   b  ", 2)]

def test_word_count():
    for text, expected in CASES:
        assert word_count(text) == expected, text
```

## Test the behaviour that depends on a decision, not the decision

```python
# Change detector: fails when the constant is retuned, never when retrying is broken
def test_max_retries():
    assert MAX_RETRIES == 5

# The behaviour that depends on it
def test_a_failing_call_is_retried_five_times_and_no_more():
    client = FailingClient()
    with pytest.raises(UpstreamError):
        fetch(client)
    assert client.attempts == 6  # the first call plus five retries
```

## The mock earns no assertions; never patch the code under test

```python
# Asserts on the stand-in: true while the stand-in is present, whatever the page does
def test_page_has_a_sidebar(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(page, "render_sidebar", lambda: "<sidebar-mock>")
    assert "<sidebar-mock>" in page.render()

# Replaces the function the change is about: the test cannot see a regression in it
def test_discount(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(pricing, "apply_discount", lambda total, code: 90)
    assert checkout_total(100, "TEN") == 90

# Real code; only the external rate service is replaced, with a complete response
def test_discount_is_applied_before_tax():
    rates = FixedRates({"TEN": Decimal("0.10")})
    assert checkout_total(Decimal("100"), "TEN", rates=rates) == Decimal("90")
```

## Mock the slow level, keep what the test depends on

```python
# The stand-in swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads
monkeypatch.setattr(catalog, "discover_and_cache", lambda: None)

# Only the slow server start is replaced; the config write stays real
monkeypatch.setattr(server_manager, "start", lambda: FakeServer())
```

## Confirm the red

```text
FAILED tests/test_slug.py::test_spaces_become_hyphens - AssertionError: 'hello world' != 'hello-world'
```

This is a red: the test ran to its assertion and the message is the expected one. These are not:

```text
ERROR tests/test_slug.py - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'slug'
ERROR tests/test_slug.py::test_spaces_become_hyphens - TypeError: slugify() takes 0 positional arguments
```

An import or signature error shows that the test cannot run yet, not that the behaviour is wrong. Make it run, then watch it fail on the assertion.
